desc: Upon gathering leaders from each warrior band beneath one tent, we will elect the Khāghān who will lead our hordes to victory. In this ''kurultai'', the fate of our people is decided, and leaders will be chosen from among those who think themselves worthy of leading us.
entities.name: Kurultai

desc: The nobility will always be rather sensitive about protecting their privileges. It would go far towards winning their loyalty if said privileges were to be guaranteed forever.
entities.name: The Kutnohorian Deal

desc: Karvuna has built its power upon the sea rather than the fertile plains, drawing upon a mix of Bulgarian, Greek, and Italian sailors. By fortifying the limestone cliffs of the coast, we will create a series of naval bases that will allow us to dominate the Black Sea trade routes between the Danube delta and Constantinople. This maritime focus will provide us with a unique identity within the Bulgarian world, prioritizing naval superiority and trade over the traditional feudal concerns of the interior.
entities.name: Karvunan Maritime Heritage

desc: Given our small land area, our rulers understand the need for powerful friends and trade partners. By granting these allies exclusive trading rights in ports like Varna, the Despotate will gain access to modern Western naval technology and financial credit, as well as potentially powerful naval protection against our enemies. This alliance will transform Dobruja into a cosmopolitan trade hub, where the wealth of the Silk Road will be exchanged for the grain and furs of the north.
entities.name: Looking for Friends

desc: Karvuna will establish a permanent, state-run Admiralty to oversee the construction of modern deep-water warships and the training of a professional officer corps. Shifting away from small galleys, we will begin building frigates and small ships-of-the-line capable of projecting power as far as the Aegean and the Sea of Azov. This naval modernization will ensure that we remain a major maritime player, capable of defending our trade interests against our enemies.
entities.name: The Black Sea Admiralty

desc: As a maritime state with a relatively small land population, Karvuna has refined the art of 'contract warfare' by formalizing a permanent Condotta with the Italian maritime powers. Under this arrangement, we provide them with fortified warehouses and naval bases in the Black Sea, and in return, the Italians provide a professional corps of heavy crossbowmen and expert siege engineers for the Despotate's defense. This symbiotic relationship allows Karvuna to punch far above its weight in land battles, utilizing Western tactical innovations and professional discipline to defend its coastal strip while the native Bulgarian sailors dominate the waves, effectively outsourcing its land defense to the most skilled mercenaries in the Mediterranean.
entities.name: The Condotta of Varna

desc: To maintain its status as the premier trade hub of the Black Sea, we will promulgate a revolutionary legal framework known as the 'Code of Karvuna', which will grant extraterritorial rights and religious freedom to recognized merchant nations. Regardless of their faith or origin, any merchant operating within our ports will be judged by a commercial court of his peers rather than by local feudal lords. This atmosphere of legal predictability and tolerance will attract a massive influx of capital and expertise, turning Karvuna into a huge hub where the wealth of the silk and spice roads will be reinvested into the state's infrastructure and military-industrial complex.
entities.name: The Cosmopolitan Code of Karvuna

desc: To cement our position as the premier commercial hub of the Balkans, we will declare Varna a free port, exempting international merchants from most traditional duties in exchange for a flat transit fee. This policy will attract a massive diaspora of merchants, bankers, and insurers, making Varna the 'Venice of the Black Sea' and the financial capital of the Bulgarian world. The resulting wealth will allow us to maintain a professional army and a world-class navy, ensuring that our coastal state remains a wealthy and independent power in an age of giants.
entities.name: The Free Port of Varna

gate: num of non rural GREATER THAN

desc: Combining sap from lacquer trees in multiple layers, gives the produced items their signature glossy finish, in a Lacquerware Artisans' Guild. Such sought-after high quality items include furniture, ceremonial boxes, and more. Lacquerware is highly valued for its beauty and resilience.
entities.name: Lacquerware Artisans' Guild

desc: Refinements of the process of painting and applying the lacquer make Lacquerware cheaper and quicker to produce.
entities.name: Lacquerware Manufactory

desc: It is common for armies to have to march great distances in order to reach their enemy. As such, long marches are a staple of our military training regimen, accustoming our fighters to walking long distances and still arriving fresh for the battle.
entities.name: March Training

desc: An army on the move is vulnerable, and prone to disorganization. Training our troops to march in an organized and coordinated manner ensures that they will retain their battle formations, even if attacked while moving.
entities.name: Coordinated March

desc: Our armies on the march is a sight to behold. Their training and discipline shines when they march in unison into battle, unfazed by any previous long march.
entities.name: Unrelenting Advance

desc: Managing armies becomes increasingly more complex as they become less reliant on levies. A key aspect of this is improved organization of armies on the march, which helps the troops to be more prepared if a battle occurs.
entities.name: Organized Army March

desc: Our people coexist with fellow men and women of many faiths. This diverse social composition is embedded in our legal frameworks and beliefs. Together, we are stronger!
entities.name: Land of Many Religions

desc: By portraying our colonies and the surrounding unclaimed lands as places where anyone can make their fortune, we will rapidly increase emigration to our colonial holdings. This means the nation will spend less money encouraging people to go there.
entities.name: Land of Opportunity

desc: The fertile lands of our domain are a coveted destination for many migrants, primarily those of lower status, seeking a better and more prosperous life.
entities.name: Land of Promise

desc: Land is not property, nor is it mere dust; it is our connection to our great forebears. From the better lands beyond, they watch over us. We must never let the connection between us be severed, and we must care for these lands in honor of those who first settled them.
entities.name: Land of the Ancestors

desc: Reunification of the Rus' is a common goal among the East Slavic rulers, and aspiring conquerors can use this as a justification of conquest.
entities.name: Land of the Rus'

desc: A new type of unit organization has been born out of Germany's constant wars: The Landsknechte, which takes the form of mixed troops formed by innovative pikemen squares, with arquebusiers supporting from their flanks, and a front line composed of the infamous ''Doppelsöldner'', 'double-pay men', carrying two-handed swords. This allows for tactics that combine close-quarters and medium-range combat.
entities.name: Landsknechte

desc: The Emperor has ordered the complete overhaul of the legal system, merging the Justinian Code with the Frankish-style ''Assizes of Romania'' into a single, unified legal body. This ''Codex Latinus'' removes the legal distinctions between Frankish and Greek subjects, creating a single class of Imperial Citizens under the Emperor's law. This legal unification is the final nail in the coffin of the old feudal order, paving the way for a truly centralized, absolute monarchy.
entities.name: Codex Latinus

desc: With the ''Frankokratia'' united under our rule, our court now meticulously blends the rigid, martial feudal hierarchies of the French and Occitan tradition with the ancient, intricate ceremonies of the Greeks. By adopting the purple robes and the dignity of the East, we command the spiritual respect of our Greek subjects while maintaining the chivalric loyalty of our Western knights. This synthesis transforms the Emperor from a mere foreign conqueror into a legitimate successor of Constantine, recognized by the Pope and feared by our enemies.
entities.name: Emperor of the Latins

desc: Dominating the narrow gates of the Black Sea allows us to levy heavy tolls on the Italian merchant republics that once dictated our fate through debt and naval blockade. The wealth of the Pontic grain trade and the Silk Road's northern terminus now flows directly into the Imperial coffers rather than Venice or Genoa, funding our restoration. We have turned the Golden Horn from a den of foreign merchants into the beating heart of a centralized, sovereign economic powerhouse.
entities.name: Hegemony over the Bosphorus

desc: The Latin Emperors have moved beyond feudal levies and now rely on a sophisticated system of maritime tariffs and transit duties. Every ship passing through the Dardanelles or the Bosporus must stop at the Imperial Customs House, where the 'Tenth of the Emperor' is collected in hard coin. This massive revenue stream allows the Empire to maintain a professional, standing army that does not rely on the whims of the nobility.
entities.name: The Golden Gate Customs House

desc: Evolving from the old Varangian tradition, our modern guard consists of professional Catholic mercenaries from across Europe, primarily French veterans and Swiss pikemen. These men are bound to the Emperor not by land or title, but by gold and a shared Crusader identity, serving as an iron fist against disloyal feudal barons. This standing force ensures that the Emperor's will is absolute, providing a stable core for the army that is immune to the whims of the high nobility.
entities.name: The New Praetorian Guard

desc: The Emperor has established a high-tier order of merit that replaces hereditary titles with service-based nobility, ensuring that the Empire's leaders are chosen for their talent. Membership in the Order is the highest honor in the land, granted to generals, diplomats, and scholars who have expanded the glory of the Latin Throne. This system creates a loyalist elite that is entirely dependent on the Emperor's favor, cementing the monarch's control over the state.
entities.name: The Order of the Star of the East

desc: Feudalism is built upon the concepts of ''auxilium'' and ''consilium'', or military aid and counsel, owed by vassals to their lords. Over this, this has created an intricate hierarchy of rank, privilege, and reciprocal duties.
entities.name: Late Feudal Relations

desc: A vast, diverse, and highly organized bureaucracy staffed by the most skilled of scribes, the Mālīye aspires to be a fundamental and incorruptible institution of the state.
entities.name: Mālīye

desc: The evolution of Polish hussars entailed the adoption of heavier armor with red and white colors. They used a longer lance of around six meters, which made their charge incredibly devastating, often breaking the morale of their foes and causing them to rout.
entities.name: Late Winged Hussars

desc: Rome has reinstated the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, once exiled and forgotten. Now restored, the Patriarch shall strengthen our influence in Rome and reinforce our role as guardian of the Church's interests in the East.
entities.name: Latin Patriarch

desc: Our realm is a crucible of noble blood from around Europe, zealous pilgrims, and old Levantine stock. Through careful governance, we shall weave together this diverse heritage into a Latin Christian society, where faith and culture go hand in hand.
entities.name: Latinate Integration

desc: New times mean new situations, and the laws that have been in place for generations may not be applicable to these new contexts. We should assign legal experts to continuously scrutinize and revise our laws, so that we can adapt them to our current times and needs.
entities.name: Legal Scrutiny

desc: Suleiman is remembered as one of the great rulers of history, a soldier, a lawmaker, and a reformer. In fact, while the West knows him as Suleiman the Magnificent, in his homeland, he is called 'The Lawgiver'. Central to his reforms was the re-examination of Ottoman dynastic law, ''Kanun'', in order to bring it in line with Sharī'ah.
entities.name: The Legal Code of Suleiman

desc: A small hospital in an isolated location, usually in the countryside, an island, or a patch of the coastline. Maritime travelers are quarantined there if they are suspected to be carriers of a contagious disease, limiting the spread of epidemics drastically in the location.
entities.name: Lazaretto

desc: Penned by royalty, the 'Book of Tournaments' is more than a manual — it is a statement of courtly pride and chivalric identity. Our nobility trains not only for war but for spectacle, and in doing so preserves martial discipline and prestige across the realm.
entities.name: Le Livre des Tournois

desc: Through the dressing process, lead ore is washed and crushed to remove impurities and separate the ore from rocks, clay and other minerals.
entities.name: Lead Ore-Dressing

desc: Leading troops is not an easy task. Strategy, tactics, mental insight — these are just some of the skills a successful leader must have. Founding officer training schools will ensure that more of our fighting men develop good leadership skills, and give us a bigger pool of expert commanders to draw from as well.
entities.name: Officer Schools

desc: Our people have been divided for too long, and we need someone strong enough to unite them and make the world tremble at our feet. The Sky will direct the acts and thoughts of this leader, and guide us to a bright future.
entities.name: A Leader under the Sky

desc: A lack of rigor in accounting is what allows corruption to thrive, and rots countries from within! To avoid this threat to our administration, we must ensure that any changes in our treasury are fastidiously accounted for.
entities.name: Meticulous Accounting

desc: Brittany has never truly been part of France Though we have been ravaged by Franks, Vikings, and the English in the past, we have, thus far, maintained our unique identity as a people. Let all of our neighbors be aware that Brittany shall remain forever free, the last bastion of true Gallic traditions!
entities.name: Legacy of Breton Independence

desc: From the Dragon Throne of China, to the various empires of Persia, to the powerful Hindu and Buddhist dynasties of India and South East Asia, Asia has been home to many mighty empires throughout history.
entities.name: Legacy of Great Empires

desc: The reign of Ivan Asen II marked a new height of Bulgarian power, diplomacy, and economic expansion. His legacy endures as a foundation for a strong and centralized state.
entities.name: Legacy of Ivan Asen II

desc: According to legend, Saint Andrew himself visited Scythia and the northern shores of the Black Sea, prophesying a great flourishing of Christianity once he reached the future site of Kyiv.
entities.name: Legacy of Saint Andrew

desc: Forged in the crucible of conquest, the Sicilian Norman army blended the unstoppable charge of Norman knights with the strategic sophistication of Byzantine, Arab, and Lombard warfare. Masters of both battlefield ferocity and tactical flexibility, they carved a kingdom at the crossroads of civilizations.
entities.name: Norman Legacy

desc: Laws and rules mean nothing if they are not compiled, standardized, and made understandable to every member of our society. By codifying clear legal standards and enforcing them uniformly, we will ensure that the principles of order and justice reach the furthest corners of our realm.
entities.name: Legalism

desc: The most important factor in efficient government is getting the right advice. We must ensure that we are as inclusive as possible when it comes to advisors, so we can maximize the number of different viewpoints we are presented with.
entities.name: Efficiency in Administration

desc: A monarchy can only survive as long as its subjects believe in the legitimacy of their ruler. There are many ways in which rulers justify their power. As time goes on, new political philosophies will arise which explain the need for a strong government in their own ways.
entities.name: Legitimization of Power

desc: Piracy is an appalling act. They are naught but worthless thieves looking to profit from the suffering of others! Formally authorizing ships to raid our enemies, however, is another matter entirely, and could be extremely profitable for us.
entities.name: Letters of Marque

requires_state: has embraced institution: Levée en Masse

desc: Warfare is an ever-evolving concept, having been studied and improved upon for generations and generations. To satisfy the need for expansion and provide the fuel necessary to fulfill these ambitions, new nationwide conscription laws will be drafted. We shall raise armies of young, unmarried recruits, the size of which will leave an indelible mark upon history.
entities.name: Levée en Masse

desc: With all men declared to be equal under our new laws, adherents of other beliefs are finally allowed full participation in our government, and may thus now contribute to our national progress.
entities.name: Liberté, Egalité, Fraternité

desc: Many leaders of the New World independence wars possessed not only the necessary military skills, but also the charisma needed to encourage morale, hold the army together, and be an inspiration to the people.
entities.name: Sons of Liberty

desc: These secular institutions are studying and meeting places for scholars and the wealthy, where they can research many topics and learn about philosophy, mathematics, religion, and science. They can be independent but will often be linked to the patronage and influence of a University.
entities.name: Library

desc: Liège has been a cultural center for centuries, the home of the most celebrated scholars in the region and the envy of our rivals. But we shall not allow ourselves to become complacent; we shall never stop improving our institutions.
entities.name: Athens of the North

desc: As part of one of the biggest dioceses in the area, there is no doubt as to the depth of devotion our people hold. We will show the world that our faith in God is as strong as our faith in our nation.
entities.name: A Devoted Land

desc: Our nation inspires artists from across Europe, who come here to create their masterworks. We will spare no expense to support these artists and attract new talent, establishing ourselves as a hub of arts and culture.
entities.name: An Inspiring Maecenas

desc: As the Crown's patrimony grows, the monarch's extended absences from the various kingdoms weaken the Crown and strain relations with subjects. To address this, the position of lieutenant emerges, acting as the monarch's temporary representative during their absences, which are not meant to be permanent. These lieutenants are not only from the royal bloodline but also from the domestic circle connected to the king's family.
entities.name: Lieutenancy

desc: The lands of the faithful have often been tainted by the presence of unbelievers, but this is why our clerics have ventured forth towards the unknown to bring the light of Jesus to distant lands. We have thus influenced these lost souls in more ways than what one might expect, even if we have not been able to make them see the error of their beliefs.
entities.name: Life Among Heathens

desc: The workshops of the Ligurian coast have developed a tradition of decorative craftsmanship — silver ''Filigrànn-a'' (''Filigrana'' in standard Italian: filigree) from the city's goldsmiths, maiolica fired in the kilns of Albisola, and intricate velvet weaves that our weavers first perfected in the fourteenth century — that found buyers wherever wealthy patrons sought something finer than the common market could supply. This artisan culture thrived in the same workshops that produced the less glamorous goods of daily commerce, giving our craftsmen a flexibility that purely luxury-focused guilds could not match. This tradition of decorative excellence attracts the most skilled artists of the age to settle among us and ensures that the work they produce commands premium prices wherever it is sold.
entities.name: Ligurian Artisan Craft

desc: Every community along the Ligurian Riviera — from the fishing harbors of Ventimiglia to the hillside villages above La Spezia — has for centuries sent men to sea in small coastal boats, mastering the currents, hazards, and weather of one of the most demanding coastlines in the Mediterranean. This tradition of practical seamanship produced sailors of unusual quality long before any of our cities built deep-water warships, and the coastal cabotage trade that these men sustained carried goods between ports that no inland road could reach as efficiently. This seafaring heritage gives our merchants a natural edge in coastal and regional trade and ensures that any galley fleet we put to sea is crewed by men who already know the water.
entities.name: Ligurian Coastal Seafarers

desc: The self-governing communes that had managed Ligurian harbor life for centuries were gradually formalized and rationalized, replacing informal custom with written charters, elected committees, and standardized administrative procedures that reduced the friction of local governance. These reformed councils gave the merchant class a structured forum for managing the affairs of their communities without dependence on noble patronage or distant judicial authority, embedding a civic competence in the institutions of every Ligurian town. This administrative tradition gives our government an unusual depth of trained civic talent and makes our institutions more responsive to the needs of the burghers who sustain our commerce.
entities.name: Reform of the Communal Councils

desc: The philosophers and jurists of ''Liguria'' have engaged as deeply with Enlightenment thought as any school in Europe, arguing that the principles of reason and natural law demand a wholesale rethinking of how states govern and laws are made. We draw on this tradition to reform our institutions from within, replacing custom and privilege with codified procedure and bringing the best administrative minds of the age into public service. This commitment to rational governance makes our laws clearer, our reforms cheaper, and our state harder to destabilize.
entities.name: The Ligurian Enlightenment

desc: The merchants of our coast did not wait for the great trading cities to invite them in — they established colonies, agencies, and partnerships in every port they could reach, from the Black Sea settlements of Caffa and Pera to the counting houses of Seville and Lisbon. These ''Colonie'' operated on networks of trust and kinship that made Ligurian credit as reliable in Alexandria as at home, and the information that flowed along those networks gave our merchants an advantage in every market they entered. This diaspora turns geography from a limitation into an asset, extending our commercial reach far beyond what the size of our fleet alone would justify.
entities.name: Ligurian Merchant Diaspora

desc: The Ligurian coast has produced navigators out of all proportion to its size — Cristoforo Colombo, who opened the western Atlantic to Castilian ambition, Giovanni Caboto, who mapped the northern coast of the New World for the English crown, and a generation of pilots whose skills carried them into every ocean that European ships reached. This tradition of producing men willing to sail beyond the horizon with imperfect charts has given Ligurian seamanship a reputation that attracts investment and patronage from courts that would otherwise never look at our small coast. This culture of navigation elevates our standing among foreign powers and draws skilled settlers and fortune-seekers to our harbors from distant lands.
entities.name: Ligurian Spirit of Navigation

desc: Under the ''Lǐ Jiǎ'' system, we are able to exercise control over our borderlands through the allocation of settled armies. By granting land and agricultural rights to our stationed troops, our borders will be safer and our authority shall be affirmed.
entities.name: Lǐ Jiǎ System

desc: With the invention of bayonets, each musketeer could also function as a pikeman. This allowed pikes to be removed from infantry equipment, and provided infantry formations with more firepower.
entities.name: Line Infantry

desc: Positioned between forest and steppe, Smolensk has long been a crossroads of war and commerce. By improving overland infrastructure and securing the arteries of caravan travel, we can reforge our role as the vital hinge between northern Rus', the Baltic, and the southern trade routes of the steppes.
entities.name: Link the Steppes Trade

desc: Good coordination between the different units of an army is crucial for it to function well. Having an organized system to relay messages between our generals and their unit officials allows all our troops to work more cohesively and respond faster to any situation.

mods.label: Movement Time when Attached to Another Unit

entities.name: Message Relays

desc: Lithuania experienced a Renaissance in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Inspired by the ideas of the Reformation and influenced by the Italian Renaissance, there was a prolific flourishing of education, arts, architecture, and literature during this era. This period will also see the creation of a written form of Lithuanian and, subsequently, the first works of Lithuanian literature.
entities.name: Lithuanian Renaissance

desc: Our vast herds of llamas provide us with fabrics to clothe ourselves, meat to feed ourselves, and pack animals to carry our burdens. They are truly invaluable.
entities.name: Llama Rearing

desc: Llamas have many functions in our society. They act as beasts of burden, as sacrifices, provide meat and wool, and even give us fertilizer for our crops with their dung. Controlling the breeding and use of llamas through government ''michis'', or herders, we ensure that the llama population is strictly monitored. This will provide an opportunity for the llama population to increase
entities.name: Llama Michis

desc: A seat of regional authority that extends the reach of the state to its most distant lands, expanding its influence beyond its immediate surroundings. When connected to the capital by the road network, they act as hubs for governance and administration.
entities.name: Local Governor

desc: Theoretically a merchant can be a citizen of the world, sailing to and from whichever port he pleases. We are going to give advantages to home merchants, for example, priority for loading and unloading of cargo, to ensure that our merchants have every incentive to bring their products home.
entities.name: Local Merchant Preference

desc: The nobles know they are simply better than other people, and will only give their loyalty to those they deem worthy. If we affirm their privileges, they will of course remember our generosity, and be more resistant to the temptations of foreign powers.
entities.name: Local Nobility

desc: Mother Earth is abundant in metal resources, but little can be done with them unless they are smelted first. As such, smelters tend to be established near where the metals are extracted, to prepare them for easier transportation and further processing elsewhere.
entities.name: Rural Smelter

desc: Governing a large nation means ruling over diverse peoples, each with their own customs and traditions. By incorporating these traditions into our official code of laws, we will create a happier and more loyal populace.
entities.name: Local Traditions

desc: People forget that the conquests of the Great Khān were as much due to superior logistics as military strength. We must emulate the techniques of the Great Khān while updating them with modern knowledge. This will give us greater scope for conquest.
entities.name: Logistics of the Khān

desc: The mulberry groves and silk workshops of Lake Como and the Lombard plain supply the courts of Europe with the finest silk cloth available, and our weavers have refined the production process to a degree that foreign competitors struggle to replicate. We protect this advantage by regulating the export of raw silk and the techniques of our master weavers, ensuring that the value-added work stays within our borders rather than leaving as cheap raw material. This control over the full production chain turns silk from a local trade into a steady source of revenue that holds its value even when other commodity prices fall.
entities.name: Masters of Silk

desc: In the foothills around Bergamo and Como, English spinning frames and power looms are replacing the old cottage workshops, and the mills running off Alpine streams have begun producing cloth faster and cheaper than any hand-weaver can match. We have invested in this transition by building company towns and bringing in foreign engineers to train our workers, turning what was a scatter of family looms into a modern industry. This manufacturing base makes Lombardy the productive heart of Italy, and the wealth it generates flows into every corner of our territory.
entities.name: La Manifattura

desc: With specific long rifles designed for hunting, our hunters will have a reliable tool for procuring food and furs.
entities.name: Long Rifle Hunting

desc: Our lands were once an important part of Lotharingia, one of the Frankish kingdoms. If we do not want to fall into irrelevance, we will need to secure our diplomatic position and establish lasting alliances.
entities.name: Legacy of Old Kings

desc: Our territory is home to many different peoples and cultures. Establishing a single state to govern this diverse population will not be easy, but we must. Only then will we be worthy successors to the Lorrainian state from which we descend.
entities.name: Land of Many Cultures

desc: We occupy vital crossing points on several rivers, which we must defend at all costs if we want to secure our independence. To this effect, we must modernize the large bridge castles of our cities, and construct large citadels at strategic points.
entities.name: Fortified Cities of Lorraine

desc: Our lands are rich in ore and coal. Extracting these resources could make us a rich country and lay the groundwork for our grand ambitions.
entities.name: Mines of Lorraine

desc: Lorraine is home to many bishops with powerful supporters abroad and within the Church itself. Cooperating with them will be useful when making our voice heard within the broader Church. Having the support of the bishops will also help us to pacify the population more easily.
entities.name: Land of Bishops

desc: The Rhône Valley has always been our artery of power, and our castles stand watch over it like sentinels of stone. These fortifications are some of the sturdiest in all of Europe, a steadfast sign of our military and engineering prowess, forever watching over our domain.
entities.name: Lords of the Rhône Corridor

desc: A breastplate made in our workshops commands a price that craftsmen in Cologne or Toledo cannot match, and our armories supply courts and captains from Portugal to Poland. We formalize the armorers' guilds under ducal oversight, setting standards that protect our reputation and keep the technical knowledge — and the profit — within our walls. This monopoly on premium military equipment brings us steady revenue and keeps our own troops better equipped than any enemy who has to import their plate from elsewhere.
entities.name: The Milanese Armorers

desc: A newly founded organization between cities with a strong Hanseatic presence, the Wendish Coinage Treaty will provide us with a strong basis to facilitate trade and commerce in our lands.
entities.name: Wendischer Münzverein

desc: We have maintained our independence by navigating the religious upheavals of the age through careful and measured diplomacy. Our commitment to our faith has been sincere but never fanatical, allowing us to preserve the goodwill of both the devout and the pragmatic. This balance of piety and prudence has become the art by which our republic endures.
entities.name: Counter-Reform Diplomacy

desc: We have encircled our city with a great ring of ''Renaissance bastions'', one of the finest defensive works of the age, completed over decades of labor and civic investment. The walls are so wide at the base that walkways run along their tops, and they have never been breached by any enemy. This fortification has allowed us to remain free where neighboring cities have fallen.
entities.name: The City Walls

desc: Our ancient ''Republican Constitution'' has survived the ages through careful governance and the determination of our citizenry to resist tyranny. When neighboring cities fell to princes and conquerors, we maintained our written laws and our councils without interruption. This enduring order gives our state a stability that larger and more powerful neighbors cannot easily replicate.
entities.name: The Lucchese Constitution

desc: Our city has long nurtured the musical arts, drawing composers and performers to its churches, salons, and public celebrations. Our chapelmasters and instrument-makers have achieved such renown that talented ''Musicians'' seek appointment here as a mark of distinction. This tradition turns our city into a stage and fills its streets with an art we have made unmistakably our own.
entities.name: The Musical Tradition

desc: We have long woven the finest ''Lucchese Silk Brocade'' in all of Italy, and our looms have made our city prosperous beyond its size. Our weavers' guilds protect the secrets of the craft and ensure the quality that commands high prices in distant markets. This mastery of cloth transforms raw threads into the foundation of our republic's wealth.
entities.name: The Silk Republic

desc: The great towers built by our noble families rise above the rooflines of our city, each one a declaration of prestige and power within the republic. The ''Torre Guinigi'' stands tallest among them, crowned with the ilex trees that have become the emblem of our city. These towers remind all who enter that our strength rests in the ambition and rivalry of citizens who have learned to compete in stone.
entities.name: The Towers of Lucca

desc: With the introduction of wind power to our sawmills, we are able to process timber into planks at a much faster rate than we could previously.
entities.name: Wind-Powered Sawmills

desc: By dedicating a portion of land to the cultivation and harvesting of strong trees, we can increase the quality and quantity of our lumber production.
entities.name: Dedicated Forestry

desc: Thanks to recent advances in toolmaking, our sawblades are sturdier than ever before and require less maintenance. This will make supplying adequate lumber for economic activities far easier than before.
entities.name: Improved Sawblades

desc: The great Luxembourg dynasty, whose very name is derived from that of our nation, is now the most important family in Europe. This has to be a sign from Heaven, and we will use this divine benediction to further extend our influence.
entities.name: Destined to Rule

desc: The impregnable position of Luxembourg, with the formation of the Bock acting as a natural fortress, is incredibly strong. Our enemies would perish in any attempt to usurp our holdings. We shall learn from nature, and construct all our fortresses so as to use the local terrain to their advantage.
entities.name: The Fortress of Europe

desc: John the Blind, the heroic King of Bohemia and Count of Luxembourg, was born in our humble realm. He died in the Battle of Crécy at fifty, having charged headlong into combat despite his blindness. His brave, honorable death will inspire our soldiers for centuries.
entities.name: Heirs of John the Blind

desc: Our forests are a vital resource, providing timber for construction and fuel for our fires. We must manage them wisely to ensure their continued abundance.
entities.name: Baltic Forestry

desc: Our network of forts and castles scattered across the landscape provides a first line of defense against invaders. These strongholds allow us to monitor and control key routes through the Baltic.
entities.name: Baltic Forts

desc: Centuries of autonomy and our harsh environment have bred separatist tendencies among regional tribes within our borders. Maghrebi administration addresses this through creating a network of regional governors, who enforce central authority and the ruler's will while respecting local customs.
entities.name: Maghrebi Administration

desc: The 'Great Charter' is a legal document that aims to protect the feudal rights of our barons against unjust taxation and legal maneuvers by the Crown. It is also one of the earliest documents to enshrine the idea of civil liberties, such as the right to a fair trial and protection from illegal imprisonment.
entities.name: Magna Carta

desc: One of the two major Smṛti texts together with the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahābhārata is an epic of ancient India. It is the longest epic poem ever written, about ten times bigger than the Greek ''Iliad'' and ''Odyssey'' combined, and it narrates the story of a dynastic struggle for the throne of the ancient Indian kingdom of Kuru culminating in the Kurukshetra War, also called Mahābhārata War. The story ends with the death of Kṛṣṇa and the end of his dynasty.
entities.name: Mahābhārata

desc: By expanding our already-growing printing industry, we can become the leading producer of books in Europe.
entities.name: Printing Shops of Mainz

desc: The citizens of Mainz have prospered under the extensive rights granted to them by Adalbert of Mainz in the early 12th century. These rights, carved into the bronze door of the Cathedral, will serve as a reminder of cooperation between the separate powers within the city, both the clergy and the citizenry.

mods.label: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

entities.name: Rights of the City

desc: Our beloved city has been described as 'Diadema Regni', the Crown of the Empire, a moniker we strive mightily to maintain. Maintaining this distinction will help us remain above other Imperial cities in terms of our prestige and political influence.
entities.name: Diadema Regni

desc: Defending our borders can be a difficult task, especially considering the river splitting our land in two. We must build an extensive network of garrisons and fortifications that can withstand our enemies.
entities.name: Garrison of the Rhine

desc: When the Rheinish League was active, we naturally assumed a position of leadership and guidance for the other members. Although the League itself has disbanded, we must do everything we can to maintain our influence over our former associates.
entities.name: Rheinish League

desc: While celebrations on Ash Wednesday are a common occurrence, they hold especially deep roots in our country. While the public celebrates the ''Fastnacht'', or carnival, with masquerade and excessive feasts, our court will engage in a special event. During the carnival celebrations, we will redistribute the roles of our court per lottery, with even the ruler having to participate. This custom of swapping roles, called ''Mainzer Königreich'', will spread far beyond our borders and help expand our cultural legacy.
entities.name: Mainzer Königreich

desc: To ensure our lands are governed reliably, even in the absence of our ruler, we should instate a vicar. Empowered with extensive rights, the vicar can rule with our best intentions and remind the common folk of our presence at all times.
entities.name: Governance of the Vicar

desc: Our country's religious unity must be defended against any threat. If we provide our armies with moral guidance in the form of military chaplains, they will be much more motivated to defend our beliefs.
entities.name: Protect Our Faith

desc: Maitreya is currently a Bodhisattva, prophesized to be the future and final Buddha of the current era. His destiny is to reestablish the teachings of the Dharma in the world after they have been forgotten by humanity, and as such he is the successor of Siddhārtha Gautama.
entities.name: Maitreya

desc: A ceremonious gate of magnificent proportions, the Bajang Ratu follows the architectural design of a ''candi bentar'', or split gateway. Using high quality red brick, the gateway is to be one of the tallest constructs across the Majapahit domain. Its usage is vital, as the structure is used for grand ceremonies of religious and political nature.
entities.name: The Bajang Ratu Gate

desc: Some of the most efficient fishing techniques are employed in local fish traps, known as Bubu. Woven soft wood, such as bamboo, they are tended to by experienced fishermen in strategic locations such as river mouths and employed intricate techniques to maximize their catch.
entities.name: Bubu & Jala

desc: Used widely across the entirety of the Indonesia, the Kabang is a versatile ship of medium size and often crafted from a single piece of wood. Beyond its role as transport of people and goods, it has come to be synonymous with sea nomads. These folk consist of populations of peasants and fishermen who used the tide and monsoons to migrate from port to port, making a living off the sea.
entities.name: Home of the Sea Nomads

desc: Contact with our neighbors in the archipelago has shown us clearly that the raw resources and unclaimed lands are ripe for the taking, promising to become secure and prosperous under our control.
entities.name: Island Colonies

desc: The Jong has proudly served our people for a long time. Its characteristic number of masts and hull are made of thick wood, making it the perfect vessel for a combination of ferrying goods across long distances, as well as troops.
entities.name: Jong

desc: Armed with rudimentary armor and their trademark blade, these warriors rely on mastering speed, ferocity, and fluent movements. They excel on close combat where the karambit's curved blade is extremely efficient at slashing, hooking, and gutting opponents. The adoption and proliferation of new formations and combat maneuvers has turned these warriors into a fabled armed force, feared throughout the archipelago.
entities.name: Late Karambit Warriors

desc: Our geographical position, complemented by our growing influence, has led to us presiding over the extensive and profitable trade network that carries Silk and spices from East to West.
entities.name: Maritime Silk Road

desc: The history of the Javanese people is an integral part of our cultural identity. To protect this identity, we must preserve the traditions upon which we built our great country.
entities.name: Preservation of Javanese History

desc: Scattered throughout Nusantara are a series of temples known as ''candi''. We should restore these temples wherever we find them to renew our people's faith.
entities.name: Restore Candi Shrines

desc: The head of our military directly answers to our ruler, and holds enough influence and power to shape the future of our realm. To ensure they understand what an important role they have been given, they are required to swear a special oath, one that underlines our dreams of conquest and bolsters our spirits.
entities.name: Sumpah Palapa

requires_state: has advance: maj the magic arrow

desc: The people that populate the Madura Strait have come to serve in our navy. Their naval prowess and great shipbuilding skills have given rise to a new kind of vessel, the Madurese Ghali. A large ship, it is used for offensive and voyager-adjacent tasks, as it will soon comprise the backbone of our fleet.
entities.name: Madurese Ghali

desc: One of the most prominent muzzle-loaded cannons of our era is the Cetbang. Armed with a cylindrical short barrel, it delivers a devastating blow with tremendous power. Such is its popularity, that it finds use in many aspects of our conduct of warfare, from protecting our ports to being the main armament of our warships and armies.
entities.name: The Magic Arrow

desc: The Makaron Nesoi, the Blessed Isles, are believed to be the ultimate destination of the most virtuous souls. Those who live lives of piety and excellence may earn their place among heroic spirits in the Elysian fields. Tales of these sacred realms inspire the pursuit of virtue, honor, and moral excellence throughout society.
entities.name: Tales of the Blessed Isles

desc: From the bazaars of Arabia to the harbors of East Asia, our merchants are a familiar sight. Their presence forms a vast network of cooperation, easing the establishment of our enclaves abroad and extending our reach into every great entrepôt of the world.
entities.name: Malay Merchants in Every Port

desc: During our time as subjects of Mali, our people learned much from their military command and combat tactics. This knowledge shall help our own infantry in battles to come.
entities.name: Malian Military Tactics

desc: As our island lies in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea, our maritime culture has shifted toward industrial ship-repair and global logistics. Our Grand Harbor will become the premier naval dockyard of the world as local artisans adapt their ancient stone-working and carpentry skills to the era of steam and iron. This industrial seamanship will turn the islands into a global coaling station and repair hub, ensuring that our fleet remains technologically superior to those of our rivals.
entities.name: Center of the Mediterranean

desc: Our culture has produced a specialized class of 'Night Runners,' or ''Bajada''. These are men with deep knowledge of the area who can navigate the island's rocky karst and sheer cliffs in total darkness. In a military context, they are the ultimate tactical couriers, slipping through enemy lines or swimming between harbor forts during blockades. This culture of stealth will allow us, if institutionalized, to develop an army of spies that no enemy can detect.
entities.name: The Bajada

desc: Our identity is centered on the ''Festa'' and religious processions, which are organized with military precision. These elaborate celebrations, characterized by grand processions, ornate street decorations, and communal banquets, serve as the primary glue for Maltese society. This culture of public piety and shared ritualism transcends class barriers, uniting the urban burghers and rural farmers in a common identity of intense religious devotion. By channeling their resources into the aesthetic and spiritual life of their local communities, the Maltese foster an incredible level of internal cohesion and social harmony, ensuring that the archipelago remains a unified and culturally vibrant society even under the pressures of external threats.
entities.name: Festa Ritualism

desc: With the rise of Mediterranean piracy, Maltese commoners are joining the fray. By granting letters of marque, we can benefit the realm by creating a class of 'Sailor-Merchants' who see the sea as a battlefield for both profit and faith. This will turn us into the 'Vikings of the South', experts in boarding actions and coastal raiding. This maritime aggression will ensure the coastline is guarded by a fleet of aggressive, privately-funded coast guards who know every hidden cove.
entities.name: The Korsa

desc: In the wake of the new threats, the informal village watch known as the Dejma is in need of modernization. We will develop a national militia system where every male between 16 and 60 is assigned a specific post. This will create a culture of the 'Soldier-Peasant', where the agricultural cycle is intertwined with military drills. This widespread martial literacy will ensure that the islands can never be taken by a surprise landing, as the entire countryside functions as a high-readiness reserve force that supports the professional soldiers of the realm.
entities.name: The Modernized Djema

desc: The Maltese landscape has become defined by the ''Raħal'' (the village), centered around a fortified parish church. Unlike European feudal manors, the Maltese village is a tightly-knit kinship network where the common people manage their own local security. This fosters a culture of the 'Watchman State', where every villager is trained to spot sails on the horizon and retreat to the ''Dejma'' (local militia) posts, turning the islands into a decentralized, self-repairing defensive grid.
entities.name: The Rahal Watch

desc: Auxiliary units that often accompanied their Mamlūk counterparts, these light and quick troops will offer great support to their parent forces on the battlefield.
entities.name: Ḥalqah

desc: Well-trained elite troops, these men have been honed to represent the best our people have to offer. Raised as slaves purchased from foreign masters, they are disciplined and taught our religious and military doctrines as they are expected to form the core of our standing army. Oftentimes, they come equipped with heavy armor and sturdy spears. Their unique helmets and presence in the battlefield is a terrifying sight for our foes.
entities.name: Early Mamālīk

desc: For well over a century the ''Casa Gonzaga'' has ruled Mantua not as conquerors but as lords whose claim rests on a compact of mutual benefit with their subjects — a legitimacy that no merely military power can purchase and that we have maintained by never treating the city as a resource to be extracted. We sustain this standing through three interlocking channels: the church patronage that binds our subjects through shared devotion, the formal dynastic titles that give our rule a legal foundation that rivals cannot challenge, and our deliberate respect for the commune traditions that Mantua's citizens still recognize as their inherited right. This triple foundation of faith, dynasty, and civic compact gives our state a legitimacy that is felt by every subject rather than merely proclaimed from above, and makes our rule more stable than any arrangement built on force alone.
entities.name: The House of Gonzaga

desc: Our court has become one of the great magnets of artistic talent in the peninsula — painters, sculptors, and architects arrive already knowing that Mantua rewards ambition and that the work produced here will reach the eyes of every prince who sends an envoy to our door. We formalize this tradition of patronage into a deliberate policy, maintaining stipends and workshops that keep multiple artists resident at once and ensuring that the work they produce reflects the standing we intend to project. This culture of ''Mecenatismo'' reduces the cost of maintaining artists and draws talent of the highest quality to settle permanently among us rather than passing through for a single commission.
entities.name: Gonzaga Patronage of the Arts

desc: When Claudio Monteverdi staged ''L'Orfeo'' in our Palazzo Ducale for the Accademia degli Invaghiti, he gave the world its first fully realized opera — a work in which voices, instruments, and drama were fused into a form that audiences immediately recognized as unlike anything they had heard before. Mantua was the city where this transformation happened, and its court was the institution that made it possible, providing Monteverdi with singers, players, and the sustained patronage without which neither the rehearsals nor the score could have materialized. This primacy in the birth of opera makes our court the acknowledged origin of Europe's most powerful new art form, and the artists trained in its shadow carry our reputation to every stage they subsequently inhabit.
entities.name: Monteverdi's L'Orfeo

desc: Federico II Gonzaga commissioned Giulio Romano to build a pleasure palace on an island at the edge of the city, and what emerged was the ''Palazzo Te'', one of the most inventive buildings of the Renaissance — a work of architecture that quotes the classical tradition with such knowing wit that scholars have argued over its ironies ever since. The frescoed rooms, from the giants collapsing in painted ruin to the horses of Federico's stables rendered with life-size confidence, are the most daring decorative programme in northern Italy. This extraordinary achievement deepens our cultural tradition and gives the works produced under our patronage a singular character that collectors and courts seek out above the more conventional output of our rivals.
entities.name: Palazzo Te

desc: The lowland plain that surrounds Mantua on three sides is among the most fertile land in Italy, and we have made systematic investment in its management the foundation of our domestic economy — draining marshes, expanding irrigation channels, and regulating the reclamation of new land at the margins of the lakes that define our geography. The result is an agricultural capacity that grows reliably each generation, supplying our city with food surpluses that sustain a population larger than our politics alone would justify. This patient cultivation of the ''Pianüra Padâna'' (''Pianura Padana'' in standard Italian: the Po Plain) ensures that our subjects eat well in difficult years and that our treasury collects the taxes of a prosperous countryside.
entities.name: Po Valley Agriculture

desc: We establish a formal studium in Mantua, drawing teachers of law, philosophy, and the arts from the great universities of the region and providing the sons of our burghers and minor nobility with an education that was previously available only to those wealthy enough to travel to Bologna or Padua. The institution links Mantua to the network of European learning that flows through the great schools, bringing the latest ideas in jurisprudence, theology, and natural philosophy into our city rather than letting them arrive years late through correspondence. This ''Studium Mantovano'' raises the literacy of our governing class and ensures that new ideas take root among us as quickly as they spread anywhere in Italy.
entities.name: The Studium Mantovano

desc: As our nation has undergone fundamental transformations, so will our army. The world has opened itself to us, and new challenges will appear on the horizon. If we want to survive in this new paradigm, we have to be ready to act.
entities.name: Manchu Reborn

desc: The Manchu alphabet has emerged, combining Classical Mongolian characters with Jurchen phonetics. This unique writing system facilitates left-to-right vertical column writing. With diverse letter forms and contextual adaptability for initial, medial, final, and isolated positions, it preserves the most subtle nuances of our language.
entities.name: Manchu Script

desc: As the Khān commands, gods do. The unity of our people comes from their loyalty to our great leader. Only someone capable of bending the will of those loyal to the ruler is worthy of our devotion.
entities.name: Mandate of the Khān

desc: The Mandekalu Levies are the backbone of the Malian military. Freemen of the Empire are called to arms in times of war, and it is a great honor for them to participate in these battles with their own weapons.
entities.name: Mandekalu Levies

desc: Whether pagan or Muslim, Mandinka men have been the greatest fighters the Sahel has ever seen. The courage of our troops is admirable, as is their pride. When the Mansa raises an army, not only is it the largest in all the Sahel, it is the best!
entities.name: Mandinka Warrior Spirit

desc: Recent technological advances in mechanization have facilitated the rise of concentrated production facilities in the form of manufactories. These businesses have helped us greatly improve the rate and quality of production.
entities.name: Manufactories

desc: Our citizens are the power base of our overlord's trade empire. Foreign goods are delivered to us, which we then mold into finished products.
entities.name: Imperial Manufacturing Center

desc: The ground shakes as our warriors perform the ''Haka'', their fierce cries and synchronized movements echoing across the battlefield. This intimidating ceremonial war dance emboldens the heart of every warrior, granting a significant morale boost to land forces.
entities.name: Ceremonial Haka

desc: The so-called 'Declaration of the Independence of New Zealand' is a document that once and for all establishes a unified Māori state that is independent. With the wording fully understood by all sides, our chieftains may finally unite, and be free from foreign interference.
entities.name: He Whakaputanga

desc: By perfecting the art of growing and storing ''kūmara'' tubers in specially-constructed ''rua'', or storage pits, we can ensure that our bellies are filled even in the harshest of winters.
entities.name: Rua Kūmara

desc: With the intricate curves and spirals of ''Tā Moko'', we ritualistically etch pigment into our very skin, transforming our bodies into living tapestries of honor and history.
entities.name: Tā Moko

desc: We know that by preserving and nurturing ''Te Reo'', our sacred language, we maintain a vibrant connection to our culture and traditions.
entities.name: Te Reo

desc: Strength and unity come from knowing one's ''Whakapapa'', the intricate web of genealogical connections that binds an ''iwi'' together. This deep understanding of collective ancestry fosters a united front against all adversities.
entities.name: Whakapapa

desc: The many maple trees in our country produce great quantities of sap, which can be collected and boiled to create a delicious sweet syrup and other confections.
entities.name: Maple Syrup

desc: Accurately drawing the borders and landmarks of a country is much more than art — it helps us collect information about other nations for strategic purposes. By knowing where important places are exactly, we can not only better coordinate attacks, but also gain more knowledge about our own territory. As the elders often say, knowledge is power.
entities.name: Mapmaking

items.label: March to the Sound of Guns

desc: With the steady growth of our army, our logistical needs have changed. Our generals will adopt 'march to the sound of guns' doctrine — ordering dispersed forces to move toward battle independently when they hear fighting. This enables rapid reinforcement without having to await orders.
entities.name: March to the Sound of Guns

desc: By granting considerable autonomy to vassals in border regions, these 'Marcher Lords' will be able to raise large military armies to support us in our wars.
entities.name: Marcher Lords

desc: The authority of the Margrave is greatly threatened by the ever-increasing power of our Estates. The Estates are of great benefit to our nation, but the threat they represent to our base of power necessitates the creation of a new council, one which reduces the very real power that the estates hold over our nation into more of an advisory position for the Margrave. This way, we may continue to enjoy the benefits of our Estates while having fewer concerns about their needs.
entities.name: Geheimer Rat für die Kurmark

desc: Our dedication to the Virgin Mary must remain a central pillar of our worship.
entities.name: Devotion to the Virgin Mary

desc: Marines are military units that specialize in amphibious operations. They can be used in raiding shores and boarding enemy vessels, while still seeing action on land.
entities.name: Marine Regiments

desc: As commerce grows, so does the need to more quickly and efficiently transport greater quantities of goods. As such, those invested in maritime trade will spare no expense in building the bigger fleets they can afford.
entities.name: Trade Fleets

desc: As our knowledge of the world grows, so does the need to learn even more about it. From the far seas to the east to the new coasts in the west, the length at which we must sail has increased, and thus so has the need for a bigger fleet.
entities.name: Exploration Fleets

desc: Given the advances of the last century, it seems like the world has become smaller rather than bigger. Countries that had no contact until now are instead engaging in constant diplomatic and commercial relations. As a result, bigger and better fleets are needed to be able to maintain all those overseas connections.
entities.name: Global Fleets

desc: As maritime trade expands, with our ships ferrying goods back and forth in greater quantities and to more distant shores than ever before, the need to maintain a consistent flow of commerce also increases. Organizing convoy trade fleets will allow a more stable circulation of trade ships.
entities.name: Convoys

desc: Trade convoys are obviously a very juicy target for any pirate. Ships full to the brim with goods and coins are a booty that few will let pass through. Thus, providing those trade convoys with defense armament to deter those attacks is vital. Having the trade fleets be accompanied by frigates or any other armed vessel ensures their safety.
entities.name: Armed Convoys

desc: The seas are constantly crossed by eager merchants searching for the best profit. This naturally evolves into certain routes becoming more established and frequented than others, with the most popular ones seeing a steady steam of ships sailing back and forth.
entities.name: Established Routes

desc: In our kingdom, Salt is worth its cost in gold. But south of us, in the great forests of the Ashanti and the Yoruba, salt is worth considerably ''more'' than gold. Luckily for us, we have our own supply of Salt, and enough gold to obtain as much as we could ever want. Perhaps we could find yet more markets of people for whom Salt is more valuable than gold?
entities.name: Markets for Salt

desc: Verona has become a destination that the educated aristocracy of Europe cannot complete their travels without visiting — English lords, French scholars, and German princes make their way to the Arena, the Roman theatre, and the Gothic tombs of the Scaligeri, spending freely and writing the city into the correspondence of every court on the continent. Their accounts turn Verona into a byword for Italy's layered heritage, a city where Roman, medieval, and Renaissance civilization can be read in a single afternoon's walk through streets that belong to no single century. This steady stream of wealthy and influential visitors enriches our treasury, opens diplomatic conversations that our size alone would never invite, and builds a reputation for civilization that travels far ahead of our armies.
entities.name: The Grand Tour

desc: A martyr is someone who understands that dying on behalf of their faith is the highest of honors. The people of our land keep their faith close to their hearts, and are always keen to join our cause. If they die as martyrs, it is an honor and not a tragedy.
entities.name: Martyrs

desc: We have, up to now, been very selective about who can serve as an enlisted member of our military. We only took the poorest and most desperate — basically, the people no one else would miss. Now, though, we shall open up the ranks to everyone who wishes to serve and has no significant wealth to speak of.
entities.name: Mass Army

desc: Let us mass our artillery in a single grand battery. Its destructive power will blast a hole in the enemy lines!
entities.name: Massed Battery

desc: Trading in cloves holds much wealth for us and our people. By securing the lands and seas from which these spices flow, we stand at the center of a trade that spans the world, and no merchant can ignore the allure of these goods.
entities.name: Masters of Spice

desc: The heart-vein of our Sultanate is the river Nile. Traversing our nation, its touch creates our most fertile lands, and its life-bringing waters of the river channel prosperity and ample wealth throughout our domain.
entities.name: Masters of the Nile

desc: Improvements to the weapons produced by our gunsmiths will also provide our hunters with better tools to bring home ample furs and wild game.
entities.name: Early Hunting Guns

desc: Every local shrine and temple has its own festivals and celebrations. The people are always eager to participate, for it is their chance to offer devotion and gratitude towards their local protector ''Kami''.
entities.name: Matsuri

desc: The size and depth of the Spanish Square gave it staying power, but made it slow and cumbersome to maneuver on the battlefield. It also led to a large percentage of troops being inactive during battles. Maurice of Nassau, the Stadtholder of the Netherlands, reduced the total number of men in the formation to make it more mobile and reduced its depth, so it maintained the same firepower and shock value.
entities.name: Maurician Infantry

desc: The new sciences have given us a number of different ways to describe and measure the world around us. However, we cannot know all of the resources that could be at our disposal until we have thoroughly searched all our lands for minerals, counted every last subject, and assessed every last enterprise. Let us command out scholarly experts to conduct a thorough survey — first of our nation, then of the entire world!
entities.name: Measuring the World

desc: The religious upheavals of the age demanded a visual response, and our cities answered with an explosion of chapels, altarpieces, and sacred facades that transformed every urban skyline into a theatre of piety. Confraternities, civic councils, and wealthy patrons competed to commission the most luminous images, the most dynamic sculptures, and the most persuasive devotional paintings their treasuries could afford. This tradition of sacred patronage sustains our artists, fills our streets with devotional imagery, and signals to every visitor that our culture lives at the center of a confident and expressive spiritual life.
entities.name: Baroque Sacred Patronage

desc: The Italian Wars proved that medieval curtain walls could not stop artillery for more than a morning, and our hill towns responded by turning their greatest natural asset — the ridge, the spur, the ravine — into systems of angled bastions and compact ''Rocche'' that made each town a distinct tactical problem. Architects and military engineers rebuilt our defenses in stone and rammed earth, positioning artillery platforms at the angles that most terrified attacking batteries. This tradition of fortification adapted to terrain makes our territories harder to overrun and far costlier for any invader to hold.
entities.name: Bastioni e Rocche

desc: The rationalist currents of the eighteenth century found in our communal tradition a soil already prepared to receive them — cities long accustomed to debating their own governance, recording their decisions, and holding their magistrates to account in writing. Reform-minded governors and learned academies pushed for clearer codes, more orderly urban plans, and more predictable administration across the towns and countryside we govern. This embrace of rational governance makes our institutions more efficient and our subjects more inclined to see the state as a partner in civic life rather than an obstacle to it.
entities.name: Enlightenment Civic Reform

desc: The Holy Years that Rome declared every quarter-century brought pilgrims from every corner of Latin Christendom onto the roads of our territory, and the ''Grand Tour'' that followed brought a second wave of wealthy and curious northerners willing to pay generously for comfort, guidance, and company. Our inns, markets, and workshops learned to serve an international clientele, and the money they left behind flowed through every level of our economy. This tradition of hosting the faithful and the curious makes our cities prosperous far beyond what local production alone could sustain.
entities.name: The Jubilee Economy

desc: Before most of Europe had thought to write its customs down, the cities of our region had already codified their laws, established their councils, and set out the duties of every citizen and magistrate in the pages of the ''Statuto''. From Ancona to Viterbo, these documents were revised, contested, and renewed by each generation, creating a living tradition of civic argument that neither feudal lords nor passing conquerors could wholly extinguish. This heritage of written law makes our institutions resilient and our burghers invested in the city they help to govern.
entities.name: Lo Statuto del Comune

desc: The university at Perugia, founded in 1308, placed itself under civic rather than ecclesiastical authority, and the schools that followed across our region trained the lawyers, notaries, and administrators who carried the business of the Italian commune forward. Our cities offered the libraries, the patronage, and the debating culture that drew men of learning from across the peninsula, making legal and philosophical training as natural a product of central Italy as any craft. This tradition of learned governance gives our officials a preparation in law and argument that their counterparts in more purely feudal regions struggle to match.
entities.name: Studio Generale

desc: Specialized sites for medical training, these schools are where scholars go to learn about the human body, diseases, and how to treat and prevent them.
entities.name: Medical Schools

desc: The healing properties of certain plants have helped our people overcome different diseases for centuries. Infusions of certain leaves have even been said to lengthen the lives of our people.
entities.name: Medicinal Infusions

desc: With a military elite in place to govern our society, the next stage of development is to build a literate class of administrators. Typically, these roles will be filled by drawing from the clergy.
entities.name: Medieval Administration

desc: Over the past centuries, land armies have become more professional and well-organized. Better systems are in place to support the mix of levies and professional soldiers that now dominate the battlefields, and the infantry is slowly but steadily gaining power, poised to overtake that of the cavalry arm.
entities.name: Medieval Military

desc: Meḥmed I issued a decree demanding that only Turkish be spoken in courts, dervish lodges, assemblies, and public squares. This act rejected Persian and Arabic dominance in elite circles and laid the groundwork for a uniquely Turkmen cultural policy.
entities.name: Meḥmed Bey's Firman

desc: The Meißen Lion, also known as the ''Markmeißnische Löwe'', holds a special place in heraldry. Representing the Wettin dynasty's symbol of power, an armored black lion with a red tongue gazes to the left on a golden field. Its image appears in various forms, including on painted tombstones, ensigns, helmets, coins, and seals, symbolizing the affiliation of the city of Meissen to the ''Mark Meißen'' and adorning the coats of arms of numerous towns and communities. Some link it to the recolored Thuringian lion.
entities.name: The Meißen Lion

desc: The ''Meißner groschen'' will serve as our national currency. This coin is based on the ''Prague groschen'', which we will replace. This new large groschen will mark the beginning of a new era in the history of our coinage and will let us better control its influxes.
entities.name: Meißner Groschen

desc: Saxony is the first country in Europe to produce Porcelain, which will bring wealth and prestige to the Wettin court.
entities.name: Meissner Porcelain

desc: As legend goes, the timid mouse deer sought refuge in what would later become our domain. Our beggining is humble, as little more than a fishing village clustered beneath the shade of the Melaka tree. From these roots shall grow a people that will one day shape the entire region.
entities.name: The Melaka Tree

desc: It is no secret that other nations envy our literary accomplishments and enlightened past. They seek to hire tutors from our court, eager to sink their claws into the knowledge that gave rise to powerful empires and carved the cultural landscape of the entire continent. It is through these men of letters that our neighbors will come to fall in love with our history and become educated in our ways.
entities.name: Men of Letters

desc: The orders of our faith, who have taken vows of poverty and live itinerant lives, have brought assistance to many remote parts of our country. We should support their efforts as much as we can without disrupting their holy missions.
entities.name: Mendicant Orders

desc: Naples, inspired by the influential maritime republic of Amalfi, boasts a vibrant culture of trade. Strategic ports, including the city of Naples itself, served as vital hubs, connecting the kingdom to distant lands and fostering economic prosperity through commercial exchanges and the flourishing exchange of goods and ideas.
entities.name: Mercantile Spirit

desc: It is well understood that mercenaries do not work for free. By promising fair compensation and a share of the plunder, we can assure their loyalty more easily, and ensure the most skilled companies will be willing to work for us
entities.name: Ensure Mercenary Payments

desc: This allows us to make use of the numerous traders lusting for fame and fortune, eager to offer their services for a chance to search and explore new trade routes.
entities.name: Merchant Adventures

desc: Let every merchant ship fly our emblem with pride and know that our navy will always be there to protect them, if needed.
entities.name: Merchant Marine

desc: Merchants and their trading contribute substantially to our national income. However, merchants are also excellent sources of information, as they are often in the position to observe first-hand what circumstances our neighbors are in. By giving them official roles in the government, we can exploit their knowledge and mobility to our own ends.
entities.name: Merchant-Officials

desc: With the emergence of new ideas about commerce and economics, the local businesses have joined together to form a business network that can further their interests and protect their rights against political entities and foreign influences.

mods.label: Max Level of Trade Company Headquarters

entities.name: Chamber of Commerce

desc: The confraternities of merchants allow our traders to organize, share profitable trade route information, and join forces when buying and selling in foreign markets.
entities.name: Merchant Guilds

desc: The expansion of markets overseas — and the associated expenses and risks — require the creation of merchant associations that share the burden of trading in these new lands.
entities.name: Merchant Companies

desc: The rising prominence of long-distance trade has led merchants to innovate new ways of making the most of their activities through partnerships. The most common kind is having one partner invest a sum of money in the trading expedition, while the other does the traveling and procurement of goods to be sold after their return.
entities.name: Merchant Partnerships

desc: Merchant ships have become a common sight in our waters. Our traders have so many vessels going back and forth that they have effectively formed their own fleet.
entities.name: Merchant Fleets

desc: The frequent failures of chartered companies have led to the development of a new business model: limited companies, where shareholder liability is limited to their initial investment. This protection from unlimited debt makes such partnerships far less risky and more attractive to potential investors.

mods.label: Max Level of Trade Company Headquarters

entities.name: Limited Companies

desc: Michelangelo Merisi, born in a small town near Bergamo, developed a way of painting light and shadow so direct and brutal that it made the work of every other school look artificial by comparison. His followers spread the ''Chiaroscuro'' technique from our cities to Rome, Naples, and Madrid, and patrons have started to commission works explicitly in the Lombard manner. This reputation turns our cities into destinations for collectors and scholars, and the artists we train are in demand everywhere they go.
entities.name: The Lombard Chiaroscuro

desc: A steady flow of trade and commerce is a sure sign of a healthy economy. With our merchants focusing on keeping the trade flowing, we can establish a tradition of and reputation for lively commerce, making it easier to attract foreign trade to our nation.
entities.name: Merchant Traditions

desc: The patterns of trade had been seriously disrupted, possibly due to plagues and pandemics. Now trade is slowly beginning to recover.
entities.name: Merchants and Trade

desc: Bustling with traders, these quarters house shops and storage, serving as the economic heart where deals and exchanges flourish.
entities.name: Merchant Quarters

desc: Merit is not exclusive to the upper echelons of our society. It can be found everywhere, even among the humblest individuals. By creating standardized exams that measure this merit, effort, and overall competency, we can find intellectual jewels hidden in plain sight, and properly appoint them for the betterment of our nation.
entities.name: Meritocracy

desc: Metallurgy, the art of manipulating and working metal, stands as one of the defining capabilities of advanced civilization. Metal tools and weapons are far superior than their stone counterparts, enabling both workers and soldiers to operate with better efficiency.
entities.name: Metallurgy

desc: We have made ''Casale Monferrato'' the heart of our state, a city that grows in commerce and craft under the shelter of our rule. The merchants and guilds of the city bring life to its streets and revenues to our treasury, and its position on the roads between great powers makes it a natural gathering place for trade. This city is our richest possession and the proof of what sound governance can build.
entities.name: Casale Monferrato

desc: We have transformed ''Casale Monferrato'' into a fortress city whose walls and bastions are among the most formidable in the peninsula. The citadel's deep ditches and angled walls are designed to exhaust any siege and bleed any attacker who thinks to take it quickly. This fortification has made our seat of power into one of the great military prizes of the age, too costly to assault and too important to ignore.
entities.name: The Casale Citadel

desc: Our court has become a gathering place for artists, scholars, and musicians drawn by the patronage and refined taste we offer. We prize the ''Arts of the Court'' as instruments of prestige, and the works produced under our roof reflect well on our name wherever they travel. This investment in culture returns in reputation what it costs in coin.
entities.name: The Court Culture

desc: We have survived between greater powers through the arts of flexibility and careful friendship, never placing our trust entirely in any single alliance. By maintaining a reputation for reasonableness and good faith, we have made ourselves useful to those who might otherwise simply absorb us. This ''Diplomatic Resilience'' is our oldest strategy and our most reliable one.
entities.name: The Marquisate's Resilience

desc: The rolling hills and fertile valleys of our marquisate yield harvests that sustain our people and support a growing population of farmers and rural craftsmen. Through careful management and investment in our lands, we have expanded the reach of our agriculture into slopes and terraces that once lay idle. This ''Agricultural Transformation'' brings new settlers to our countryside and new revenues to our state.
entities.name: The Monferrato Agricoltura
