desc: The ''Divya Upadesh'' lays out nine principles that form the core of political and national life in Nepal, as well as guidelines for successful foreign policy. It encapsulates centuries of Nepali thought on governance, war, and peace. Following these principles, Nepal shall be able to avoid the subversion of nearby empires and marauding foreigners.
entities.name: The Divya Upadesh

desc: The more punishment our ships can take, the more they can dish out. Let us ensure that we have a ready supply of the finest seasoned oak for our warships.
entities.name: Oak Forests for Ships

desc: One of the most important festivals in our culture, Obon is the time to honor the dead, and our ancestors in particular. During the celebrations, offerings of food and ritual dances are performed. People also light fires and lanterns to guide the souls of the dead back home for the celebrations, and once again back to the land of the dead.
entities.name: Obon

desc: Obsession with birth and privilege has made this country weak, and the rise of self-made powerful clans throughout the realm has clearly proven how useless such notions can be. Let us take this lesson to heart, and allow success and skill be the guiding principles for who should rise to command our armies. Strong leadership is a requirement for rapid expansion.
entities.name: Oda Generals

desc: Japan is a land of castles and fortifications. It is through the construction of strong defensive positions that one can assert influence both over the political realm and the routes vital to military campaigns. This learning is one we must take to heart. It is also through our castles that we impose our presence and power upon the common people. At all times, we must prioritize the reduction of enemy fortifications and the erection of our own in strategic locations.
entities.name: Influential Strongholds

desc: Western missionaries brought many ideas and techniques to our land, and unlike the Buddhist sects of old, they have no previous ties to corrupt landowners or rebellious cities. We should welcome these foreigners into our cities, and see what benefits they could bring to our court.
entities.name: Patronization of the West

desc: It is clearly our destiny to hold all the country within our grasp. None shall resist our authority, and all under Heaven will bend to our military might.
entities.name: Tenka Fubu

desc: The advent of firearms has and will continue to revolutionize warfare in Japan, and through mastering these new weapons, we can dominate any battlefield. In order to increase the rate of their fire, our arquebusiers will form ranks, allowing one line to fire while two others reload.
entities.name: Triple Firing

desc: Despite having an illustrious lineage, our clan is not considered particularly relevant, threatening, or interesting to outsiders. Their underestimation of our strength and cunning will soon prove to be their undoing...
entities.name: Uninspiring Clan

desc: The era of gunpowder and military innovations is upon us, and with it comes a renewed interest in and vitality to the conduct of warfare. To further our glory, we must diligently ensure high standards for our offensive armed forces.
entities.name: Offensive Army

desc: It is a precept of Buddhism to make offerings to the Three Jewels in order to accumulate merit. These offerings may be material or non-material, and some monastic communities depend completely on food donated by their followers for their survival.
entities.name: Offerings

desc: Each year a portion of our ritual offerings is dedicated to the three Moirai, the Fates who govern destiny itself. Clotho the Spinner, Lachesis the Alloter of life's portion, and Atropos the inevitable end preside over the completion of every mortal life according to the cosmic order. In many theological traditions their authority is considered primordial, sometimes even surpassing that of the gods.
entities.name: Offerings to the Moirai

desc: The Nakasendō is one of the most important routes between central and eastern Japan. Controlling it also means controlling the trade that flows through it.
entities.name: Improving the Nakasendō

desc: Horses from the Kiso area are our preferred breed. They are not as high nor as fast as other types, but they make up for it with high stamina, and are sturdy enough to survive in the mountains.
entities.name: Kiso-Uma

desc: Traditional forms of many things are highly valued in our society. We have formalized the official system of martial arts and etiquette for samurai since the founder of our clan, Ogasawara Nagakiyo, originally developed a special school, where all samurai should go to learn the proper techniques.
entities.name: Ogasawara-Ryū

desc: Our clan belongs to a sub-branch of the Minamoto, and rules Shinano Province as its ''Shugo''. Our land is mountainous and unwelcoming to many. For our people, however, it has for a long time been an integrated part of our defenses against outsiders. Let us take this experience with us wherever our armies go, and make sure to always obtain thorough information about the terrain in any region where we do battle.
entities.name: Shinano Shugo

desc: An eight-mode system of writing music, the Oktōēchos has been the system used for writing religious chants and music for the Church for centuries. It is the foundation of Orthodox chant, although with some variations between cultures.
entities.name: Oktōēchos

desc: Despite not being an island, our land is factually isolated from the rest of Arabia due to the surrounding deserts. As such, we have learned how crucial it is to have access to the sea, and how useful it will be for us if we take that option away from our enemies.
entities.name: Land Isolation

desc: Our sailors are used to navigating far and wide upon the seas, but control of the gulf surrounding us is what allows such travels. We must always stand ready to defend our waters against any foreign threat.
entities.name: Control of the Gulf

desc: Our nation is at the back of the ample and hostile deserts of Arabia, but the sea to our east allows us to circumvent them. It is by sea, not by land, that we will need to perform our diplomacy, trade, and expansion.
entities.name: Gulf of Oman

desc: The principles of our faith originate from the will of the gods and are interpreted through priests, seers, and acts of divination. Through prophecy and sacred interpretation mortals attempt to understand the divine order of the cosmos. Yet the surest path to moral virtue remains piety, reverence, and the careful avoidance of destructive hubris.
entities.name: On Hubris & Morality

desc: Coming from China centuries ago, the theories of Yīn and Yáng evolved in Japan into Onmyōdō. Expert practitioners, called ''onmyōji'', deal with the purification and exorcism of evil and vengeful spirits, as well as with divination, astronomy, and the study of nature.
entities.name: Onmyōdō

desc: What makes a man willing to fight and die for his country? Is it his faith? Loyalty to his nation? Or is it simply a desire to protect his family? In the end, the answer does not matter, as everyone has the duty of serving under our banner.
entities.name: Open Levy Standards

desc: The vast seas promise us great riches and new opportunities for trade on distant shores.
entities.name: Overseas Exploration

desc: Magnificent and ornate buildings specialized in the display of opera performances and usually built thanks to the patronage of wealthy and influential individuals.
entities.name: Opera House

desc: Victory is not just won on the battlefield, but also in the drawing rooms. Our advancement of reason helps our people shrug off the effects of temporary setbacks, and prepare instead for our inevitable victory.
entities.name: Optimism

desc: Long before our rise, the Orang Laut roamed the straits as masters of wind and tide. Now, by learning their ways and employing a select few, we guide traders through the narrow waters and shield our coast from pirates. Such vigilance ensures that all who sail to Malacca arrive safely.
entities.name: Orang Laut

desc: Establishing loyal Orders will undoubtedly increase our local defensive capabilities and make it easier to recruit able-bodied fighters.
entities.name: Order Headquarters

desc: Upgrading our government's infrastructure is a costly business. However, if we structure the process correctly, we can do it for less expense.
entities.name: Organized Construction

desc: Mercenary captains are a canny lot. They will try to coax two commanders in the same army into a bidding war over their services. We must streamline our mercenary recruitment process to prevent this sort of trickery, and to ensure we are always in the best position during negotiations.
entities.name: Organized Mercenary Payments

desc: Money is not the only limiting factor when it comes to recruiting mercenaries. The other bottleneck is finding mercenary companies who actually wish to serve with us. Thus, we must ensure our system allows every company to join us.
entities.name: Mercenary Recruitment

desc: Religion plays a major role in every society, yet not every faith has the same structure. An organized religion has its rituals and belief systems systematically arranged, and follows defined doctrines.

mods.label: Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities

entities.name: Improved Religious Organization

desc: The ''Anka'' system is our method of documenting the regnal years of our rulers. Years ending in 6 or 0 are skipped, except for year 10, which is retained. The count begins at year 2, not year 1, and always starts on the ''Sunia'', our fiscal new year.
entities.name: Anka Year System

desc: The Muslim faithful have invaded India and subjugated many Hindu residents under their gruesome rule. Yet, Orissa stands unflinching against the warriors of Islam. We are the bulwark of Hinduism, and we shall defend our traditions and culture against any foreign invader!
entities.name: Bulwark of the Hinduism

desc: The high-quality Salt of Orissa is in demand all over India. Let us do whatever we can to encourage the Salt trade so that we may grow rich from it.
entities.name: Salt Trade

desc: As technology advances, so does the number of people in our realm. Industrialization has driven significant population growth, and as such, we must expand our infrastructure to accommodate these growing communities.
entities.name: Expansion of Infrastructure

desc: Horses are not native to Orissa, and the lands here are unsuitable for raising them. Our jungles are, however, famously teeming with elephants. In the dense jungles of Eastern India, well-executed tactical cooperation between elephants and infantry can be just as deadly as a cavalry. Let us further increase the size of our elephant corps and refine their tactics, so that we will be known as a true ''Gajapati'', 'Lord of the Elephants'.
entities.name: Gajapati

desc: The Muslim threat never ceases, nor does it ever rest. We must ensure our military is ready to face and combat invaders at any and all times.
entities.name: Odia Militarization

desc: Orissa has long been divided among many different princes, but their time is over! We will take control of these lands, and appoint regional governors — ''parikshas'' — instead of allowing these petty princelings to dilute our imperial authority.
entities.name: Parikshas

desc: The glory of past dynasties is reflected by the grandeur of the temples they left behind. We should improve our many magnificent temple complexes, and construct new ones to further the development of Kalinga architecture.
entities.name: Patronized Temple Construction

desc: Orissa has been famous for its high-quality textiles since ancient times. Let us further encourage the textile guilds of Orissa to refine their methods of producing their fine Kalinga Cloth.
entities.name: Refined Cloth Production

desc: Worship of Jagannath, the Lord of the Universe, is what unites our people. Previous rulers of Orissa were even considered to be the scions of Jagannath. Our current ruler might not be one of his descendants, but we must imprint on all that our leader is the servitor of Jagannath, and that any disobedience to them equals treason against Lord Jagannath himself.
entities.name: Servitor of Jagannath

desc: It is from our lands that Coffee comes, as we have the perfect growing conditions. While it can be cultivated in other places, ours is revered for its quality and exported by the ton. We have to make this a way to channel wealth into our nation.
entities.name: Origin of Coffee

desc: There have been many schisms and divisions in the Christian world, but our creed traces its roots on the original true Christianity formulated from the First Council of Nicaea. Every split from the main branch after this is mere heresy.
entities.name: Original Christianity

desc: It has been said that Ormus is 'a vast emporium where there were peoples and goods of every description from all parts of the world' or that 'If all the world were a golden ring, Ormus would be the jewel in it'. Our realm's identity is inseparable from commerce. Indeed, ships from Gujarat, Arabia, and even China anchor in our ports, exchanging spices, Gems, Silk, and stories.
entities.name: A Vast Emporium

desc: The Persian Gulf is crossed daily by our fleets — be they traders, patrols, or armed escorts. But to match the ambitions of those who envy our position, we must expand and modernize. Let Ormus become more than just a trading post: a maritime arsenal.
entities.name: The Ormuzi Navy

desc: It is the right and duty of the ruling classes to display their power through their appearance. As such, they are wearing increasingly flamboyant attire, making use of the latest techniques to achieve vibrant and luxurious colors and patterns.
entities.name: Ostentatious Clothing

desc: The Ostrog is a small, wooden fortification which is constructed in remote territories of Russia. Due to their reliance on lumber, Ostrogs are relatively inexpensive and swift to construct.
entities.name: Ostrog

desc: Our increasing interactions with foreigners have sparked an interest in Christianity for many in our clan. The Christian people have many powerful advocates among our lords and vassals, and few are as zealous as recent converts. Let us make good use of these Christian converts, regardless of which route our own clan takes, and use their influence and zeal to further our own agenda.
entities.name: Christian Converts

desc: We have been designated ''Shugo'' of Bungo, Hizen, and Hyūga. This positions us perfectly to claim all of Kyūshū for ourselves!
entities.name: Domination of Kyūshū

desc: We have been the ''Shugo'' of Bungo since the Kamakura era. These lands are known for their highly fertile soil, and the rich harvests from this region allow us to feed larger armies than many other Daimyō can support.
entities.name: Lord of Bungo

desc: Others may denounce foreigners as barbarians, but we recognize the benefits and advantages of trading with them. Let it be known that they will always be welcome in our ports — and we will be able to expand our trade network further than our rivals.
entities.name: Welcoming the Nanban Trade

desc: The ''Birûn'', or the Exterior Service, comprises the group of administrators, military officers and religious scholars just outside the ruler's personal inner circle. Together, they make up an efficient bureaucracy inherited from Persia and the Great Seljuks, but adapted further by elements from Byzantium, making it uniquely Ottoman indeed.
entities.name: Birûn

desc: A system of tax farming where nobles purchase the right to collect revenue from parcels of land owned by the state. Muqāta'ah balances the distribution of wealth across the empire, and turns the nobility away from corruption, giving them a vested interest in supporting the state.
entities.name: Muqāta'ah

desc: A complex system of supply depots and lodgings for use by soldiers and officials, ''menzil'' waystations allow our armies to rely less on plunder, and remain well-supplied on every frontier.
entities.name: Menzil

desc: Our chronicle says we are descendants of Prince Imseong of the royal house of the ancient Baekje Kingdom, which once ruled in Korea. This legendary connection means we hold a prestigious position in East Asia.
entities.name: Descendants of Baekje

desc: In order to retain good relations with nations on the continent for the sake of our traders, we must mount constant sea patrols. As long as pirates and smugglers are common in our waters, foreigners will not trust us, and may even act against us.
entities.name: Countering Piracy

desc: Due to our location, we are the clan trading most actively with Korea, and as a result we have a near-monopoly on many exotic goods. We must do what we can to retain this favorable position, and leverage it to out-compete any upstart that might challenge us.
entities.name: Trade with Korea

desc: As our trade network expands, we come in more frequent contact with foreigners and their strange habits and faiths. Regardless of what they believe, their coin is good enough; we should appear to be open to their ideas as we are to their business if we wish to secure repeat commerce.
entities.name: Welcome the Westerners

desc: It is the holy duty of the Church to bring the light of Christ to the pagan and the infidels. We must go beyond our borders to carry salvation to every lost soul!
entities.name: Outwards Expansion

desc: Our capital and other cities are built using army camps as a model. They have wings, vanguards, and fronts. In ensuring that military thinking permeates daily life, we will improve our overall combat readiness.
entities.name: An Army Overnight

desc: Our clergy is ready and willing to spread our faith into new territories overseas. With their contribution, settling new lands will be made easier and cheaper.
entities.name: Overseas Missions

desc: Establishing colonies in distant lands is nearly always a one-way trip for those involved. Even if strange new diseases do not take you or unforgiving terrain does not starve you, the amount of time it takes to sail back means you will most likely never come home. While these realities are discouraging to some, if we remind people of the potential riches to be gained from colonial life, we can encourage them to settle lands further afield despite the dangers.
entities.name: Fortune-Seekers

desc: To expand trade, we need to extend the rights of citizenship to people who live abroad, support our trade, and are of the right social class.
entities.name: Overseas Merchants

desc: News of the discovery of distant lands has reached our nation, and our merchants are already preparing to expand their trading operations. These unexplored territories are filled with prosperous markets dripping with wealth, like so much ripe fruit waiting to be collected.
entities.name: Overseas Trade

desc: At some point, people may be discontent with our leadership — it is practically unavoidable. However, these grumblings will not grow into anything major as long as we do not let them fester. If we actively seek out those who raise their voices against us, we can nip any agitation in the bud before they have the chance to rally others around them, and thus keep the general populace content. Or at least complacent.
entities.name: Keep Agitators in Check

desc: The da Carrara family have governed Padua for over a century as lords whose authority rests on a combination of personal prestige, legal sanction from the empire, and a genuine investment in the prosperity of the city they rule. Our administration has maintained the civic institutions that the commune period established, channeling their energy into the service of seignorial government rather than displacing them, and the result is a city that functions with unusual smoothness. This tradition of ''Signoria'' that respects the civic fabric it inherits gives our urban governance an efficiency that reduces the cost of keeping our subjects settled and loyal.
entities.name: The Carraresi Signoria

desc: The medical faculty of Padua has been recognized across Europe as the most rigorous training ground for physicians since the university was founded, combining systematic anatomical study with clinical observation in a way that the great Arab compilations alone could never provide. The students who pass through its dissection theatre carry an understanding of the body more detailed and more precise than any other school in the Christian world could offer, and the physicians they become have changed how illness is understood and treated in every city they subsequently serve. This tradition of empirical medicine gives our population a resistance to epidemic disease that more superstition-dependent approaches cannot produce and deepens the literacy of every educated class the university touches.
entities.name: The School of Medicine

desc: The oldest municipal institutions of our city — the elected councils, the written statutes, the tradition of citizen participation in public decisions — have never been fully extinguished, even through the decades of seignorial government that placed a single family above them. We revive and formalize these communal structures, giving our merchants and burghers a recognized role in civic governance and restoring the sense that the city belongs to all its citizens rather than its rulers alone. This ''Comùn Padovàn'' (''Comune Padovano'' in standard Italian: Paduan Commune) channels the energy of our most active citizens into institutions that serve the state, increasing the tax revenue that flows from a population that believes in the legitimacy of what it pays into.
entities.name: The Paduan Commune

desc: The philosophy faculty of Padua has developed a tradition of rational inquiry into the natural world that operates on Aristotelian premises while reaching conclusions that trouble the Church far more than open theology might have. In Padua, it is considered legitimate to argue that the soul is mortal, that intellect is collective rather than individual, and that natural causes could explain what elsewhere requires divine intervention. This culture of secular reasoning produces lawyers, physicians, and administrators of unusual intellectual independence, trained to analyze rather than simply to accept authority. The reputation of the ''Paduan School'' makes our state a gathering point for minds that produce more careful governance, and draw scholars who enrich our city's intellectual life.
entities.name: The Paduan School of Philosophy

desc: We establish the ''Accademia Patavina di Scienze Lettere ed Arti'' to gather the leading scholars, physicians, and men of letters of the city into a single institution with the formal backing of the state — a structure that turns the individual brilliance of the university's faculty into a sustained collective enterprise capable of undertaking projects no single professor could manage. The Accademia provides a forum where the results of the university's research meet the practical needs of administration and commerce, making learned expertise available to the state at a fraction of the cost of maintaining separate advisory bodies. This institutionalization of scholarship gives our court an unusual depth of technical and administrative counsel and keeps talented men in our service who might otherwise seek the grander stages of larger states.
entities.name: The Accademia Patavina

desc: Founded in 1222, the ''Bò'' — named for the inn where its first students gathered — has never ceased to be one of the great centers of European learning, and Padua's willingness to teach subjects that more cautious universities declined has made it a destination for the curious minds of every generation. Vesalius performed his anatomical demonstrations here, Galileo lectured from its chair of mathematics, and the law faculty has trained judges and administrators across the continent. This unbroken tradition of free inquiry raises the literacy and capacity of the burgher class that relies on the university and attracts scholars whose presence keeps the city's intellectual life in motion.
entities.name: The University of Padua

desc: Paiks are foot soldiers of India who are renowned for their offensive and defensive versatility and their skill in archery.
entities.name: Paik Infantry

desc: The Paik System is a corvée labor system where capable adults, the so-called ''Paiks'', are obligated to serve in the state militia in exchange for farmland.
entities.name: Paik System

desc: The only effect of bloodshed is to cause further bloodshed. Therefore, we need to be a forgiving ruler, and reconcile with our enemies to establish a lasting peace in our territories.
entities.name: A Mild and Calm Ruler

desc: Rich in theological scriptures of several Christian denominations, the ''Bibliotheca Palatina'' is one of our most prized possessions. Protection of the knowledge and the cultural value contained within must be a high priority, so that we are able to keep relying on its documents.
entities.name: Protect the ''Bibliotheca Palatina''

desc: By erecting multiple castles in key positions along the Rhine, we will be able to exert and expand our control over both the river and the trade flowing through it.
entities.name: Castles on the Rhine

desc: Although our territory is small, the sunny banks of the Rhine are perfectly suited to cultivate vineyards and orchards. With some effort, these could sustain our local economy by producing wine.
entities.name: Vineyards and Orchards of the Rhine

desc: Our administration is skilled in handling multiple disconnected territories without losing our grasp on them. With that, we can build a strong bureaucracy capable of handling even the most difficult tasks.
entities.name: Consolidate the Territories

desc: No matter their denominations, all Christian people must be welcomed in the towns and cities of our lands. While others may decide to suppress their religious minorities, our tolerance will ensure a steady stream of immigrants into our territory, and we shall benefit from their presence.
entities.name: Palatinate Tolerance

desc: The Reformation has created many discussions around the nature of our faith. We should invest into a comprehensive catechism, to which our people will be able to adhere.
entities.name: Heidelberg Catechism

desc: To govern well, our rulers must receive a comprehensive education in humanist ideas. To this effect, we must hire renowned humanists for the education of our rulers and heirs, while also focusing our court on these principles.
entities.name: Humanist Education

desc: When our peasantry rises up against our nobility, they unmistakably rise up against our own rule. However, we should not excessively punish those who revolt. With mild consequences, everyone will be more in alignment with our authority.
entities.name: Forgiveness for Peasants

desc: Originating from the dynastic coat of arms of the Wittelsbach family, the Palatine Lion is the centerpiece of our legitimacy. Displayed with a red crown, it signifies our role as the Imperial Vicar and Arch-Steward of the Holy Roman Empire. As long as the Palatine Lion is proudly displayed on our crest, our legitimacy will not come into question.
entities.name: Palatine Lion

desc: By virtue of having our territories disperse, we are vunerable to attacks from several foreign powers. Constructing many fortified outposts within our lands will buy us time to raise an army and repel any attempt to take over one of our many disconnected territories.
entities.name: Local Fortification

desc: A significant part of the Romantic movement is centered around Heidelberg. We should capitalize on this phenomenon, and support these and other artists in order to bolster our global recognition.
entities.name: Support the Romantic Movement

desc: Although there are many different canons in Buddhism, depending on the school, the Theravāda Pāli Canon is the oldest and most prestigious. Other schools have created their canons from a mix of texts with various sources, but the Pāli Canon has remained unchanged since the times of Ashoka 'the Great', and contains the words of the Buddha himself. It has also served as the foundation of many other schools.
entities.name: Pāli Canon

desc: We may not have a very robust manufacturing industry, but one thing we do have in abundance are palm trees. Sturdy enough to support construction and shipwrighting, but flexible enough to be shaped by our artisans, mastering the use of this unique lumber will help us expand our seafaring activities, improve production, and ultimately line our pockets.
entities.name: Palm Tree Masters

desc: The Pan Amalgamation is an improvement of the Patio Process that speeds up processing.
entities.name: Pan Amalgamation

desc: Sunda lies at the crossroads of great empires: India, China, and the Islamic world. By positioning ourselves as an indispensable node in this network, we secure access to goods, ideas, and partners across Asia turning our harbors into gateways of prosperity.
entities.name: Pan-Asian Trade

desc: The Bishop of Rome holds a position unlike any other in Christendom — not merely the highest-ranking prelate but the ''Vicarius Christi'', whose pronouncements on matters of faith bind every Catholic ruler and kingdom whether they welcome them or not. We cultivate this authority as much through spiritual relationship as through institutional power, presenting ourselves as the father of all the faithful rather than simply their ecclesiastical superior, which gives rivals pause before they choose open confrontation with the See of Rome. This dual standing as institutional head and spiritual father generates a continuous religious influence across Europe and makes antagonizing us a costly act for any ruler who depends on the loyalty of Catholic subjects.
entities.name: Head of the Church

desc: The political earthquakes of revolution and war have stripped away much of our temporal power, yet the fundamental need of states for religious legitimacy has not diminished — and it is precisely this need that we leverage in the formal treaties we call ''Concordats''. We negotiate with each sovereign power separately, trading some degree of independence in administrative matters for legally binding recognition of Church rights, the security of our seminaries, and the formal standing of Catholic clergy within their borders. This system of bilateral agreements transforms every Catholic state from a potential adversary into a partner bound by treaty, giving us a diplomatic reach that no army could have preserved.
entities.name: The Concordat System

desc: When the Papacy speaks in matters of faith and governance, it speaks with an authority that no secular ruler can claim — the force of divine mandate expressed through the ''Bulla Papalis'', a formal pronouncement that carries the weight of scripture to every Catholic court in Europe. We reinforce this with a legal tradition that stretches back to the donation of imperial authority itself, giving us not only the prestige of God's representative but the documented right to intervene in secular affairs, sanction wars, and call the powerful to account before a higher court than any king commands. This standing as both spiritual voice and legal arbiter means that when we recognize a cause as just, allies gather faster and rivals hesitate longer than they would for any purely secular power.
entities.name: The Word of the Lord

desc: Paper is the cornerstone of every realm, as it is used in every aspect of it, from administration to education and even trade. Thus, the Papermakers' Guild ensures the proper standard of production and volume, as well as a unique technique that involves the soaking, pulping or pressing of basic supplies such as linen, cotton or other plant fibers.
entities.name: Paper Guild

desc: Rag Paper, made from cotton unfit to be processed or otherwise used, set new standards for quality and durability.
entities.name: Rag Paper

desc: Utilizing fiber plants like hemp or paper mulberry, paper production will become widely available across the world. While cheap to produce, this paper is lacking in quality.
entities.name: Fiber Pulp Paper

desc: Using widely available softwood, paper will be easier and cheaper to produce than ever before.
entities.name: Wood Pulp Paper

desc: The increasing demand for Paper due to the printing industry forces innovative methods to up the production of Paper as well.
entities.name: Paper Manufactory

desc: Utilizing Cloth made from Cotton, a Paper Mill will be able to produce higher quantities of paper.
entities.name: Paper Mill

desc: Paper is a necessity for all types of advanced accounting, administration, and diffusion of knowledge. The Paper Workshop specializes in the creation of new Paper with lump, Fiber Crops and Lumber.
entities.name: Paper Workshop

desc: Parma's tradition of self-governance runs deep, forged in the era of the Italian communes when the city fought alongside its neighbors to defend their liberties against imperial ambition. We draw on this inheritance to structure the relationship between the crown and our urban communities, offering protections and recognized rights in exchange for the taxes and soldiers that sustain the state. This compact roots our authority in consent as much as in force, making our government a more stable and cooperative partner for all who live under it.
entities.name: The Commune of Parma

desc: A generation of reformers has convinced our court that the old machinery of government — its privileges, its exemptions, its slow customary procedures — is an obstacle to the welfare of our subjects rather than for their protection. We systematically replace custom with codified law, bringing reason to bear on taxation, education, and the management of public affairs. This commitment to rational governance makes our state more efficient, our laws more predictable, and our subjects more willing to trust that the government works in their interest.
entities.name: The Enlightened Duchy

desc: The cured hams and aged wheels of cheese produced in the lowlands around our city have become luxury goods traded across the continent, arriving in courts and counting houses as emblems of the finest the Po plain can offer. We protect and formalize the production of these goods, regulating the standards that make them exceptional and ensuring their export enriches our treasury as much as it delights our customers. This reputation for culinary excellence turns a humble agricultural tradition into a lasting source of commercial and diplomatic prestige.
entities.name: Prosciutto e Parmigiano

desc: The ''Bishop of Parma'' has long wielded an authority that rivals the secular power in this city, guiding its spiritual life through some of the most remarkable religious buildings in northern Italy. We choose to align ourselves with this institution rather than resist it, channeling its influence toward the stability and devotion of our people. This partnership between crown and church strengthens the faith of our subjects and gives our government a source of moral authority that no military force can easily replace.
entities.name: The Bishop of Parma

desc: The elevation of our city to the capital of an independent realm marks a new chapter for Parma — no longer a possession passed between greater powers, but the seat of a recognized territorial state with its own traditions and ambitions. We move quickly to establish the institutions and ceremonies of sovereignty, giving our subjects a clear identity and our neighbors a clear interlocutor. This consolidation of legitimate authority makes our state harder to absorb and easier to govern.
entities.name: The New Duchy

desc: Parma will be transformed into a laboratory for theatrical wonder, culminating in the construction of the first permanent proscenium theater. By establishing the picture-frame stage, Parma will create a literal and symbolic boundary between the audience and the divine artifice of performance. Our obsession with the scena — integrating complex hydraulics and ingenious pulley systems — will elevate opera from an academic experiment into a supreme spectacle of state power. This architectural breakthrough will turn us into a global magnet for scenographers, setting the technical standard for the modern opera house.
entities.name: The Opera Obsession

desc: Rivalries among royal offspring are not uncommon, as each one would like to be the ruler one day. To avoid such in-fighting, some monarchs choose to divide their territories and titles among all their sons, so that all of them are satisfied with a more or less equal share of the inheritance.
entities.name: Partition Inheritance

desc: Orthodoxy contains some movable feasts around ''Pascha'', Easter, organized in the Paschal Cycle. The ten weeks before Pascha are called ''Triodion'', while the fifty days after Pascha are called ''Pentekostárion''. This cycle marks the most important celebrations in the liturgical year.
entities.name: Paschal Cycle

desc: As the spiritual heart of the Frankokratia, Patras has evolved into a sovereign ecclesiastical principality similar to the Prince-Bishoprics of the Holy Roman Empire. The Archbishop wields both the crozier and the sword, ruling his lands through a ''Synod of Defense'' that merges religious law with feudal military obligation. This unique status allows us to mobilize the peasantry through religious fervor, viewing every border skirmish as a localized Holy War.
entities.name: The Church-State of Saint Andrew

desc: Patras has secured the right to mint its own coinage, the ''Patrine Soldo'', which is recognized for its stable value across the Aegean. By acting as the central bank for the Frankish Morea, the Archbishop exerts a powerful economic influence over secular lords. We control the pulse of trade through the purity of our silver.
entities.name: The Patrine Mint

desc: The purported relics of Saint Andrew attract thousands of Catholic pilgrims who seek safety in the East, and we have established a network of fortified 'Hospices' to protect them. By charging a modest 'Protection Fee' for passage and lodging, the Archbishopric funds the maintenance of a standing army of Crusader-Monks. These funds are also used to beautify the city, making Patras the 'Rome of the East' and a beacon of Latin architecture.
entities.name: The Pilgrimage Tolls

desc: Our ports have been declared 'Neutral Holy Ports', where merchants of all nations — Catholic, Orthodox, or otherwise — may trade in safety. This sanctuary status has turned our ports into the primary neutral ground for Mediterranean commerce. Even in times of total war, the trade of Patras continues to flow, protected by the Archbishop's ban.
entities.name: The Port of Sanctuary

desc: The Archbishop has established a school to train clergy in the art of international negotiation and secret correspondence. Our 'Black-Robed Diplomats' serve in the courts of Europe as the eyes and ears of the Latin East. This clerical intelligence network gives Patras a level of geopolitical influence that rival kingdoms envy.
entities.name: The Seminary of Diplomats

desc: To counter the influence of the Orthodox world, the Archbishop has established the first Greek-language Catholic printing press in the Peloponnese. We produce Bibles and liturgical texts that use the Greek language but adhere to Latin dogma, slowly winning the 'War of the Word' among the literate Greek classes. This cultural offensive reduces the risk of rebellion and integrates the Greek population into the Latin social hierarchy without stripping them of their linguistic heritage.
entities.name: Uniate Liturgical Printing

desc: The Patio Process consists is a method of refining low quality silver and gold ores with a chemical solution based on mercury to catalyze the amalgamation reaction.
entities.name: Patio Process

desc: The abolition of Romuva, a faith embraced by our ancestors, has shaken the very foundations of Lithuanian society. Yet, in order to secure a brighter future, we have chosen the path of Orthodoxy and fully celebrate our new identity. But if we are to be successful in that, the religious authorities of our newfound Orthodox faith must maintain autonomy from foreign patriarchates in order to avoid external interference.
entities.name: Patriarchate of Lithuania

desc: Our quest towards cultivating a culturally sophisticated society begins here. Our artistic creations will go down in history as the most marvelous wonders of this era.
entities.name: Patron of the Arts

desc: Lombard merchants and bankers have established themselves across European cities for generations, lending to courts and trading houses that find no more reliable source of credit anywhere else. By formalizing this reputation through regulated exchange houses and letters of credit with fixed terms, we make our financial network a deliberate instrument of the state rather than a scattered collection of private ventures. This reach into foreign treasuries gives us a voice in the courts of Europe that our military strength alone could never secure.
entities.name: The Lombard Bankers

desc: ] has a solid paved surface which is much better for travel.
entities.name: Paved Road

desc: The rulers of Piacenza have governed a state cobbled together by nepotism and held together by the ruler family's unusual combination of military ruthlessness and administrative intelligence, and it is the latter quality that has proved more durable. We commit to a systematic reform of our fiscal and administrative institutions, bringing the practices of the most efficient Italian states to bear on a territory that has been run too long on personal authority rather than institutional procedure. This ''Riforma Amministrativa'' rewards our most capable subjects with advancement based on competence rather than connection and gives our burgher class a stake in the efficiency of a state whose tax collection finally rewards those who produce rather than those who extract.
entities.name: Piacentine Administrative Reform

desc: The tradition of legal learning in Piacenza predates the great universities of the region — it was from our city that glossators and jurists spread across the peninsula, carrying a deep knowledge of Roman law that formed the intellectual foundation of Italian governance for centuries. We revive this tradition by establishing a formal collegium dedicated to law and civic administration, drawing students from the city's burgher families and producing a trained administrative class capable of managing the legal and fiscal apparatus of a modern state. This ''Collegium Placentinum'' raises the literacy and competence of our governing class and gives our legislation a clarity and consistency that looser institutions cannot achieve.
entities.name: The Collegium Placentinum

desc: Piacenza governed itself as a commune long before any lord arrived to claim it, and the institutions of that self-governance, including the elected consuls, the municipal courts, and the tradition of written statutes enforceable by citizens, survived every change of regime by adapting rather than resisting. We draw on this deep civic tradition to rationalize the administration of our city, reducing the friction that unwritten custom creates and giving the urban population a structure of governance they recognize as legitimately their own. This revival of ''Communal Institutions'' makes our state more stable and our subjects more willing to meet their obligations without expensive coercion.
entities.name: The Commune of Piacenza

desc: The combination of the Po river for transport, the foothills for timber and water power, and a burgher class long accustomed to trade has given Piacenza the natural preconditions for early industrial development that many larger cities lack. We invest in the workshops, the credit institutions, and the labor market reforms that allow these preconditions to generate a sustained expansion of manufacturing rather than the scattered craft production that has been all most of our towns could manage. This commitment to ''Nuova Industria'' draws workers from the countryside, expanding our urban population and the income base from which our state draws its revenues.
entities.name: New Industry of Piacenza

desc: The countryside of Piacenza has long produced soldiers of a quality that exceeds what the city's modest size would predict. Men raised on Po valley farmsteads and in the Apennine foothills endure a campaign without growing restless and hold a line without breaking, and we invest in the training, wages, and officers that turn these qualities into professional discipline. This ''Soldatesca Piastentìna'' gives our armies a hard core of experienced infantry who hold their cohesion in the conditions that break less committed formations.
entities.name: Piacentine Soldiery

desc: Our city's position at the crossing of the Po has made it one of the most contested strategic prizes in northern Italy, and we have responded by investing in a fortification worthy of the target we represent. The citadel we build is not merely a refuge for a garrison but a self-sufficient fortress capable of sustaining a siege while the city outside it negotiates its own terms — a design that forces any attacker to reckon with a layered defense rather than a single wall. This ''Cittadella'' makes Piacenza expensive to take and expensive to hold against us, reducing the willingness of larger powers to treat our city as something that can be absorbed by a single campaign.
entities.name: The Citadel of Piacenza

desc: Before we had painted our greatest canvases or trained our most celebrated condottieri, we had already declared our ambition in water and stone — the ''Fontana Maggiore'', sculpted by Nicola and Giovanni Pisano and fed by a new aqueduct the whole commune funded, rising at the heart of Perugia as proof that no city in central Italy was richer, prouder, or more capable of collective ambition. The fountain gathered every saint, every trade good, and every classical virtue into a single monument and said with marble what no charter could say as well. This civic statement draws pilgrims and merchants to our center and tightens our hold over the streets they fill.
entities.name: Fontana Maggiore

desc: When the Pope imposed his salt monopoly, our people took up whatever weapons lay to hand — hence the papal mockery that named our uprising the ''Guerra delle Forche'', the War of the Forks. We lost that war and were humiliated — the Baglioni expelled, the Rocca Paolina built directly over their palaces as a stone declaration of contempt — yet the defeat calcified into something more durable than pride. This bone-deep suspicion of outside authority makes every Perugian hill a natural fortress and every invader understand that whatever they take from us will cost more to hold than any strategic advantage can justify.
entities.name: Guerra del Sale

desc: Pietro Vannucci — the ''Perugino'' — built the most admired workshop in Umbria within our walls, and his students fanned across Italy carrying the grace of the Umbrian style wherever commissions took them. Raphael came here to learn at his feet before Rome claimed the greater man, and the city that taught the teacher of Raphael carries an artistic reputation no rival in our region can easily dismiss. This tradition of workshop teaching and intensive apprenticeship makes our city a magnet for painters, patrons, and the steady flow of commissions that follows wherever skilled hands gather.
entities.name: School of the Perugino

desc: Our city's emblem is the ''Griffin'', and nowhere has it been carried further than on the banners of the Baglioni condottieri who sold their swords — and won wars — across the length of the peninsula. Perugia produces soldiers the way Florence produces painters — in quantity, at quality, with an instinct for command honed by centuries of factional street-fighting and seasonal raiding. This martial tradition breeds officers who inspire loyalty and soldiers who hold their nerve when less experienced men break.
entities.name: The Griffin Companies

desc: When revolution swept across Italy, our ancient university responded not by retreating into its medieval privileges but by opening its doors to the sons of merchants and artisans who would carry the new politics forward. The faculty of the ''Università degli Studi di Perugia'' produced the lawyers and pamphlet writers who made the Risorgimento possible in Umbria, turning a scholastic institution into an engine of civic transformation. This capacity to translate learning into organization means that no reform our government wishes to pursue will lack for educated men who know how to carry it out.
entities.name: The Old University

desc: Long after our political independence was absorbed into the Papal States, the ''Accademia del Disegno'' and the learned societies we maintained under papal patronage kept our intellectual and artistic culture alive — training the officials, theorists, and artists who staffed institutions far beyond our own borders. Every great power on the peninsula knew that Perugian training produced reliable men, and the steady demand for our graduates made our academies prosperous even as our political leverage diminished. This tradition of practical learned culture sharpens every instrument of governance we exercise and ensures our city punches above its political weight in the councils that matter.
entities.name: Umbrian Academies

desc: Our merchants have established connections to the rural settlements within and beyond our borders. As a result, they are able to secure better prices for food than would otherwise be expected.
entities.name: Peasant Connections

desc: The position of the Commoners is not only reinforced by their privileges, but also by our laws.
entities.name: Rights of the Commoners

desc: Peel Towers were developed to mitigate the dangers of life in our borderlands. They serve as protection against incursions of hostile raiding parties, sheltering both people and valuable livestock, and are a fast way to alert neighboring towns of approaching hostile armies by being a high place to light signal fires.
entities.name: Peel Towers

desc: We are the followers of Allāh, the only true God, and abide by His Word. All those who believe in Him are our brothers and sisters in His eyes.
entities.name: People of Allāh

desc: Our artisans are renowned far and wide, and it is said that they cannot leave a surface undecorated. Let us make the most of this reputation, and promote their creations as much as possible.
entities.name: People of Ornamentation

desc: We are a people shaped by wind and tide. From childhood, we learn the ways of the monsoon, the pulse of the straits, and the call of the open ocean. Our sailors carry this knowledge into every voyage, earning renown across the archipelago for their courage and mastery.
entities.name: People of the Sea

desc: Whether we take up arms on a search for prestige, to instill fear in our foes, to take captives for sacrifice,  or simply to acquire wealth, our people are accustomed to a continuous state of warfare, enduring its hardships with more resilience than members of other nations.
entities.name: People of War

desc: The fertile volcanic soil of the Sundanese highlands is perfect for growing the prized spice, black pepper. Traders from across the world seek our peppercorns for their potency and aroma. We must capitalize on this natural treasure to expand our influence through spice.
entities.name: Pepper of the Parahyangan

desc: Cultivating flowers and extracting their essence, the Perfumery produces a luxury good for the wealthy.
entities.name: Perfumery

desc: The Scaligeri have claimed the title of ''Capitano del Popolo'' not as a temporary office but as a permanent grant rooted in commune law, framing every military campaign as the defense of civic rights rather than dynastic ambition and making it far harder for rivals to cast our wars as mere aggression. Cangrande della Scala built his reputation on exactly this legitimacy — riding out against Milan, Venice, and Padua while presenting each conflict as a just cause — and we formalize his example by keeping the city's councils engaged in decisions that other lords make alone. This combination of legal standing and public mandate makes rivals reluctant to antagonize us openly, since any attack on Verona reads as an attack on the commune itself.
entities.name: Perpetual General Captain of the People

desc: Persian has served as our administrative language for quite some time, a legacy stemming from our ancient roots. This has helped us transcend the social and cultural barriers that often arise in highly diverse nations like ours.
entities.name: Persian in the Court

desc: From now on, the most heinous criminals will be executed personally by the ruler. With this, people will know that we are an orderly nation committed to justice, and they will show the appropriate obedience to the law.
entities.name: Personal Executions

desc: A small hut outside the of the borders of a community, where the sick and diseased are confined against their will to avoid the spread of plagues to the rest of the citizens.
entities.name: Pest House

desc: Alchemists and physicians are exploring new compounds and chemical mixtures in their search for remedies. Some of these early pharmacists have developed treatments for common illnesses like fevers, colds, and digestive problems, and their methods show promise for the future. However, there is still much to be learned, and many of these new remedies can be dangerous if not prepared correctly.
entities.name: Pharmacology

desc: Our currency may feel strange to outsiders, but ''Photduang'' have served us well for centuries. Roundish balls of silver and stamped with official marks, they serve as the basis of our economy.
entities.name: Photduang

desc: Our Church is the physical manifestation of the Body of Christ on Earth, having no difference from the one in Heaven. As such, the Church is the physical embodiment of the Lord Savior, sent for the benefit of His people.
entities.name: Physical Body of Christ

desc: The plains of the Po where they open onto our territory have long supported a class of lesser noble horsemen whose wealth depended on the quality of their horses and the reputation of their lance arm. We have organized these scattered men-at-arms into a formal cavalry, standardizing their equipment and training in coordinated maneuver rather than the individual charge that served in an earlier age. This ''Cavalleria Piemontese'' can screen our flanks, pursue a broken enemy, and fight in the loose formations that modern battlefield conditions demand, giving our armies a mobility that infantry alone cannot provide.
entities.name: The Piedmontese Cavalry

desc: A generation of engineers trained on the latest Italian treatises on fortification has surveyed every significant town in our domain and begun the work of converting the old circuit walls into a network of modern bastions — angled, low, and wide enough to mount artillery while denying the enemy any approach that our own guns cannot cover. We tie these citadels together by road and signal, so that a garrison threatened in one valley can expect support from the next. This ''Sistema delle Cittadelle'' transforms Piedmont into a country that cannot be overrun but must be taken fortress by fortress, a prospect that gives even the most determined aggressor pause before crossing our borders.
entities.name: The Citadel System

desc: The generation of reformers who have gathered around our court have convinced us that the task of government is not merely to preserve what exists but to discover what works better and systematically replace the old with the new. We open our administration to men trained in the academies and experimental societies of the age, commission reports on everything from agricultural yields to judicial procedure, and fund the education of a class of administrators who can read a budget as readily as a treaty. This ''Còrt Ëluminà'' (''Corte Illuminata'' in standard Italian: Enlightened Court) produces a state whose institutions are continuously improved by reason rather than paralyzed by custom, making our government faster, our research more productive, and our subjects more literate.
entities.name: The Enlightened Court

desc: The combination of water power from our mountain rivers, a growing population of skilled artisans in our cities, and the raw materials of the Alpine foothills has created the conditions for an early industrial transformation that no other region of Italy can yet match. We invest in the hydraulic mills, the standardized workshops, and the credit institutions that allow this productive base to expand systematically rather than grow by accident. This ''Base Industriale'' generates income from activities that were once invisible to the treasury and draws workers from the countryside into our towns, building the urban population and the taxable wealth of our state together.
entities.name: The Industrial Base

desc: For generations, our mountain lords levied troops on custom and season, calling men to arms when the harvest was done and sending them home before the first snow. We have replaced this improvised tradition with a formal ordinance that fixes the size, equipment, and training standards of our infantry and binds our cities and rural lords to consistent obligations that can be called on at any time. This ''Ordinansa Piemontèisa'' (''Ordinanza Piemontese'' in standard Italian: Piedmontese Ordinance) gives our army a professional core that holds its cohesion between campaigns, advancing the discipline and tradition of arms that lesser levies can never maintain.
entities.name: The Piedmontese Ordinance

desc: The ancient road descending from the Alpine passes into the Po plain once carried the legions of Rome; it has never ceased to carry merchants, envoys, and armies for whom the Piedmontese corridor is the most direct route between Italy and the north. We invest in the maintenance and security of these roads, building waypoints and toll stations that bring reliable revenue and ensure that goods in transit can move faster through our territory than through any rival route. This control over the ''Via d'le Gàlie'' (''Via delle Gallie'' in standard Italian: Road of the Gauls) makes us an indispensable link in the chain of European commerce, increasing the capacity of our markets and giving our envoys natural openings at the courts that depend on the roads we manage.
entities.name: The Via delle Gallie

desc: The Piedmontese cities have been formalizing great trade fairs across the region. By providing state protection and tax exemptions for international merchants, the state will turn the Alpine crossings into corridors of wealth. This will bring us riches, providing the necessary funds to purchase the loyalty of independent lords.
entities.name: Le fere dël Piemont

desc: Our administration will undertake a titanic effort to tame the waters of our main rivers: the Po, the Dora, and the Sesia. By constructing an intricate network of stone canals and sluices, we will transform the flooded plains and abundant marshes into the most productive rice and grain fields in Southern Europe. This will provide the region with a massive, reliable food surplus, allowing the population to grow and sustain a permanent standing army unaffected by foreign grain imports.
entities.name: The Canal

desc: While cultivated since antiquity, we will implement a scientific approach to viticulture in the vineyards of our region. By supporting the modernization and standardization of the vineyards and regulating the production of high-value wines (Nebbiolo), the state will ensure a luxury export that generates massive trade revenue. These measures will provide the treasury with a stable income that is immune to the fluctuations of the grain market.
entities.name: The Nebbiolo Vigne

desc: Recognizing our position as the gateway to Italy, we will begin transforming our cities into ''Piassafòrt'' (Fortress-Cities). This will require a cultural reinforcement toward living under constant threat, where city planning is dictated by the needs of artillery and garrisons. This engineering excellence will make Piedmont the most difficult region in Italy to conquer, forcing foreign powers to negotiate rather than invade.
entities.name: The Piassafòrt

desc: Specially linked to the Piedmontese countryside, villages have traditionally developed the ''Ricetto'' (in standard Italian and Ricèt in Piedmontese) — a fortified area within the town used to store the community's grain and wine and provide refuge during raids. This is not a lord's castle, but a communal asset managed by the villagers. This has allowed the peasantry to survive the frequent wars between the various nations of the area, ensuring that the state's productive capacity remains intact even during invasions.
entities.name: The Ricèt

desc: Piedmont will become the silk capital of Europe, characterized by massive silk factories (Filatoi) that will utilize advanced hydraulic machinery. This will create an early industrial culture in our towns, where a new class of technical artisans and merchants will emerge. These investments will provide the region with the capital needed to fund modern infrastructure and military upgrades, linking the Piedmontese economy directly to the global market.
entities.name: The Setajòj

requires_state: has embraced institution: Pike and Shot

desc: A new type of warfare has emerged on the battlefield: Pikemen form a defensive square, while arquebusiers fan out to the sides and front, retreating behind or inside the square in case the formation enters close combat.
entities.name: Pike and Shot

desc: Throughout the Middle Ages, the dominance of cavalry was challenged by disciplined pikemen. In battles such as Bannockburn or the Golden Spurs, the pikemen decimated the cavalry. A combination of improved training and discipline, and the addition of swordsmen to provide close combat support, has raised this formation to the peak of its efficiency.
entities.name: Pike Square

desc: In days gone by, our people would brave the high seas to establish colonies on distant shores. Let us rekindle this adventurous spirit in our people so that they sail forth again!
entities.name: Pioneer Spirit

desc: Across the workshops of Marseille, artisans stitch delicate ''boutis'' quilts in the Provencal style — treasured across Europe for their quality and charm. Much like our duchy, works of art created in our realm are composed of many parts stitched into a unified whole: a quilted land, rich in texture and culture.
entities.name: Piqûre de Marseille

desc: Centuries of scholarly excellence have made the name of Pisa synonymous with learning and refined culture among the educated courts of Italy and beyond. Foreign students and wealthy patrons prize a Pisan education as a mark of distinction, and the artistic works produced in this atmosphere of cultured ambition command premium prices from discerning collectors who associate the city with quality. This reputation for scholarship elevates our standing in foreign courts and enriches those who produce and sell the works of art our academic tradition inspires.
entities.name: Pisan Academic Prestige

requires_state: text: unlocked advance marble tradition tt
has variable: unlocked advance pis marble tradition

desc: The quarries supplying Pisa and the surrounding coast have long produced some of the finest white marble in Italy, used in the great churches and civic monuments that define our skyline. Sculptors and architects trained in this tradition have become sought-after across the peninsula, and the stone itself commands high prices from patrons who wish to build in the Pisan manner. This mastery of stone raises our cultural standing and ensures that every contract signed and shipment sold carries with it the prestige of a city that knows how to make the world beautiful.
entities.name: Pisan Marble Tradition

desc: For three centuries, Pisa stood among the dominant sea powers of the western Mediterranean, its galleys reaching every harbor from Sardinia to the Levant and its naval victories over the Saracens earning the city privileged access to markets that lesser powers could not enter. The defeat at Meloria in 1284 diminished our fleet, but could not erase what those centuries of seaborne commerce built — our captains know these waters, our traders know their counterparts in every port, and the routes that made us great are still routes that we can sail. This seafaring legacy gives our merchants an advantage in the Western trade sphere that no landlocked rival can replicate, and the memory of maritime greatness drives us to rebuild what was taken from us.
entities.name: Maritime Republic Legacy

desc: The medical faculty of the University of Pisa is anchored by the ''Orto Botanico'' — among the oldest university botanical gardens in the world — where students study the healing properties of plants and develop methods to treat epidemic disease more effectively. Physicians trained in Pisa carry this empirical tradition across the country, improving outcomes for the sick and reducing the toll that plague and pestilence exact on our population. This commitment to medical learning strengthens the resilience of our people and spreads the literacy that comes naturally to those trained in the careful arts of diagnosis and record-keeping.
entities.name: Pisan Medical Tradition

desc: The scholars of Pisa have pursued understanding through careful observation and measurement rather than received authority alone, building on a long tradition of inquiry in our ''Studio Pisano'' that spans mechanics, astronomy, and the natural arts. This empirical habit of mind has shaped not only our philosophers but our engineers and commanders, who approach problems with the same rigor that our scholars apply to the motion of the heavens. This culture of natural philosophy disciplines our military thinking and gives our forces a tactical precision that more tradition-bound armies cannot match.
entities.name: Pisan Natural Philosophy

desc: Founded in 1343 by imperial charter and rebuilt after each political upheaval that swept through Pisa, our university has trained jurists, physicians, and theologians whose careers carried the Pisan tradition of rigorous scholarship into the courts and churches of Italy and beyond. What distinguishes the ''Studio Pisano'' is not merely its age, but also its methods — the faculty has consistently attracted scholars who prefer questions to answers, building an institutional habit of inquiry that produces graduates capable of more than memorizing received doctrine. This tradition of active scholarship shapes the quality of every professional we train, raising the standard of learning across our institutions and ensuring that knowledge remains a living practice rather than a performed ceremony.
entities.name: The University of Pisa

desc: The mild climate and abundant fertile lands of the New World make the Colonies the ideal location for producing very profitable crops like Sugar and Tobacco.
entities.name: Plantations

desc: Standard volley fire involved each rank delivering its volley in one go to maximize firepower. But we have developed a different system of firing by platoon, with the idea being that one part of the regiment would always be firing at the enemy while others reloaded and got ready for the next volley. This removed time between attacks that the enemy could use to recover or otherwise gain an advantage.
entities.name: Platoon Fire

desc: The ancient trading ports founded by the Ostmen are still bustling hives of mercantile activity where the canny can get rich.
entities.name: Old Viking Towns

desc: Our boundary is defined by light defensive works of dykes and palisades designed to deter our unruly neighbors from launching their irritating raids.
entities.name: Pale Works

desc: Wealth and power are not synonyms, but they are certainly related: Not only can power make someone wealthy, but wealth can also grant someone power. We understand that well, as our wealthiest members of the population are also the ones who occupy the seats of power in our country.
entities.name: The Power of Coin

desc: Traders travel far afield, to provinces well beyond the reach of our authority, and even to the territories of our rivals. If these traders were to, perhaps, also serve as our eyes and ears, what secrets might we learn?
entities.name: Pōchtēcayōtl

desc: Since the earliest days of our nation, we have often cast our gaze beyond our borders, be it to establish profitable trade routes, placate formidable neighbors and build alliances, or even to forge robust partnerships against common adversaries. ''Poklisars'' are the ambassadors who carry out these missions in our name.
entities.name: Poklisars

desc: The Low Countries are highly susceptible to flooding, and the many disastrous floods that happened between the 11th and 14th centuries led to the creation of the Zuiderzee. This excessive flooding also caused coastal soils to become uselessly salinated. Thankfully, we now have the technology to reclaim this damaged land and use it productively for agriculture.
entities.name: Polders

desc: Christopher Polhem, dubbed the 'father of Swedish engineering, has transformed Swedish industry with his ''Machina Nova'', an innovative array of mechanical systems designed to streamline and boost production. Using intricate systems of gears, cams, and water power, Polhem has developed several machines capable of performing tasks previously done by hand, from ore-crushing in mines to textile weaving and sawmilling.
entities.name: Machina Nova

desc: Inspired by the ideals of the Italian Renaissance, we are experiencing a cultural golden age. Our literary achievements, architectural splendors, and cultivated atmosphere of religious tolerance have all led to a blossoming of culture across our land.
entities.name: Polish Renaissance

desc: By redistributing plots of confiscated lands to noble cavalrymen, we can build a new class of soldiers to defend our principality.
entities.name: Pomestnoe Voisko

desc: It is said that chaos is a ladder for those seeking higher status. For us, this ladder comes not from chaos but from order, as we have systematized pathways allowing our people to improve their social standing through merit. We not only permit such advancement; we actively encourage it.
entities.name: Social Ladder

desc: The dream of most peasants — to escape poverty and climb the social ladder — is a reality within our society. By rewarding hard work, meticulousness, and the proper embodiment of our ideals, we will never have a shortage of capable and influential people.
entities.name: Favorable Social Mobility

desc: Traditionally, our artistocrats achieved their status through military service to their ruler. However, the demands of a growing state now necessitate members of the lower nobility being promoted to higher ranks, while people from other classes, such as merchants, are elevated as nobles.
entities.name: Nobility by Service

desc: The Age of Reformation and Confessionalism have renewed interest in organized confessions, and there is demand for more clerics willing to guide their flocks through these troublesome times. These confessional clergy make religious offices much more appealing to those people seeking certainty and spiritual guidance.
entities.name: Confessional Clerics

desc: The bureaucracy is expanding to meet the needs of the expanding bureaucracy, which correspondingly increases our need for educated officials to join the administrative ranks.
entities.name: Bureaucratic Promotions

desc: The expansion of capitalism has given birth to a new age of social mobility, in which wealth is replacing the traditional hierarchies as means of determining social status. Everyone, from business moguls to clerks to industrial laborers, is eager to buy their way into the upper strata.
entities.name: Capitalist Social Mobility

desc: Just as we bring destruction to our enemies, we must bring peace to the many who reside within our borders. By upholding internal stability and encouraging talented men and women from all over our empire to plan and populate new and great cities, we will tame the steppes.
entities.name: Populating the Steppes

desc: In 1139, our brave troops defeated five Moorish kings in battle. This feat shall live on eternally in the memories of our soldiers, and they can use it as inspiration to defeat any enemy, no matter how powerful or well-armed they are.
entities.name: The Battle of Ourique

desc: Technological advancements have helped us develop much more powerful cannon, but most ships' decks cannot support their weight. By reinforcing our ships, we will be able to carry more munitions, and our navies will be feared for their awesome firepower.
entities.name: Bombardeiros

desc: Nicknamed the ''Fighting Cocks'', the ''Caçadores'' are an elite light infantry unit in the Portuguese Army who wear brown uniforms to distinguish them from regular soldiers.
entities.name: Caçadores

desc: By sending our most capable administrators to govern our colonies and outposts, we will ensure that these settlements remain peaceful and loyal to their mother nation, while we sit back and watch the profits roll in.
entities.name: Colonial Governors

desc: King Dinis laid the foundations for the Portuguese Navy when he appointed Genoese merchant Manuel Pessanha, originally Pessagno, as admiral of the national fleet. Pessanha's missions were to defend Portuguese shores from Muslim pirate raids, and to create a powerful trade fleet.
entities.name: Establishment of the Portuguese Navy

desc: Many places across our country, mainly in rural and remote regions, are becoming depopulated, with fields, forests, and mines falling into disuse. By reforming relevant aspects of our legal system, we will encourage people to remain in the countryside and restore its productivity.
entities.name: Stimulate Rural Areas

desc: Let us send forth our ''feitors'' to all corners of the East, and establish our country as the dominant trading force in the Indian Ocean. By creating a network of strong fortified trading posts along the coasts of Africa and India, we can dominate local trade without expending too many resources.
entities.name: Feitorias

desc: Our nation needs a professional army to guard the sacred borders of our glorious nation. We will reform the conscription system and train our young recruits to fulfill that duty with honor.
entities.name: Ordenanças

desc: It seems the land is not enough for part of our populace. Some people look at the sea and feel ''saudade'', as if it was a long-lost lover. The ports and docks bustle with eager sailors, all enrolling in expeditions as if they were drunk with a desire to explore the world. We will make great use of these eager seafarers.
entities.name: Pursuing the Waves

desc: For too long, our royal authority has been hindered by hapless meddling from the nobility, whose narrow local interests threaten the greater good of the realm. We will ignore the Cortes entirely, and rule without their interference.
entities.name: Royal Absolutism

desc: Our artillery corps and fortifications have long been the key to defending our land, making our small country a tougher nut to crack for enemy armies. We shall establish a military academy — the ''Academia Real de Fortificação, Artilharia e Desenho'' — to train our officers in these fields, so that they, in turn, may fashion our forts and our artillery corps into the finest in the world!
entities.name: Royal Academy of Fortification, Artillery, and Drawing

desc: Sometimes, members of slave-raiding expeditions stumble across gold and other precious metals or stones. Spreading word of these valuable discoveries should pique the interest of hardy souls who might be willing to emigrate to our colonies in search of their fortunes.
entities.name: Encourage the Bandeirantes

desc: On the banks of the Douro river, in the north of the country, grapes are cultivated to create a unique Wine fortified with spirits, which is famously known as ''Port Wine''. As we are the only nation producing this delightful intoxicant, we must not miss our chance to make scads of money from its export.
entities.name: Vinho do Porto

gate: num of non rural GREATER THAN

desc: Porcelain is a type of ceramics characterized by its strength and translucence due to the vitrification of the materials caused by high temperatures. The Porcelain Kiln specializes in the creation and decoration of such wares.
entities.name: Porcelain Kiln

desc: The production of Porcelain is the result of long alchemical experiments, allowing an alternative to the expensive import from overseas.
entities.name: Porcelain Manufactory

desc: The Port Authority oversees maritime traffic, enforcing regulations, collecting tariffs, and ensuring the safe flow of goods and business through the harbor.
entities.name: Port Authority

desc: Not every scallywag is worthy of being a captain; only the most experienced and skillful of them will lead our vessels. Such salty seadogs should be capable of safely finding their way back to port even in the fiercest of storms.
entities.name: Experienced Captains

desc: Maintaining regular patrols along all our coasts will ensure that our administrative authority is felt everywhere, even in the farthest regions.
entities.name: Coastal Patrols

desc: Designating our ports as official merchant zones for incoming cargo is a move that will certainly increase the mercantile significance of our territory, albeit at the expense of our neighbors and foes alike.
entities.name: Port Customs

desc: The port of Aden has been a nexus of trade for millennia — its natural harbor welcoming ships from India, Egypt, and East Africa. If properly supported, it can once again become the cornerstone of our maritime economy and the pride of the Red Sea.
entities.name: Port of Aden

desc: To reap the full financial potential from trade, we need ships and any cargo they carry to be safe when docked in our ports. We must ensure that any areas that merchants consort in are free from petty crime.
entities.name: Port Security Improvements

desc: In declaring Livorno a ''Porto Franco'', we open our harbor to merchants of every faith and nation — Armenians, Jews, Greeks, and Flemings all welcomed without the religious conditions that other Mediterranean ports impose. This freedom draws skilled traders and financiers whose settlement enriches our city and swells our trade routes with goods that more closed ports cannot handle. This cosmopolitan harbor transforms Livorno from a modest fishing village into one of the most dynamic commercial ports in the western Mediterranean, drawing population and capital to our shores.
entities.name: Porto Franco

desc: With communications being what they are, it is difficult to ensure that our diplomatic dispatches arrive in a timely fashion. Creating a network of post offices and courier rest stops will make it easier for our voice to be heard in distant lands.
entities.name: Postal Service

desc: Since maize grows poorly in the high plateaus of our land, we have learned to rely instead on the highly nutritious roots of a local plant. With increased production, we can feed our people and our warriors with this easily maintained crop.
