desc: Every human was created equal to the Creator, and therefore we understand that their beliefs, even if wrong, can be accepted as a means to eventual conversion to the one true faith.
entities.name: Ideas of Tolerance

desc: With the expanding of our economy, no longer can our people rely on artisan-made tools. The establishment of proper workshops for the production of tools for our population and business has become a necessity.
entities.name: Tools Workshop

desc: As the place of our court, our capital should also bask in the glory and magnificence of our rule. No other town or city should come close to it in majesty and grandeur.
entities.name: Splendorous Court

desc: From all settlements of our country, both rural and urban, none is more important than our capital. Being the place of our court and the source of our power, it clearly deserves some preferencial treatment compared to other settlements.
entities.name: Capital Primacy

desc: It is unquestionable that any substantial aglomeration of people and residences makes a settlement quite different from the countryside. Inheriting from the traditions of Roman self-administrated cities, we can provide such settlements with special laws and privileges, thus making the difference more clear and providing advantages for their populace.
entities.name: Borough Privileges

desc: As our country grows, so does our capital, requiring constant revision and update of the laws affecting it. Only with a functioning capital, with laws and privileges perfectly suited to its size and importance, can our country continue growing.
entities.name: Developed Capital

desc: As the source of our government, our capital is the heart of the nation itself. This fact alone makes it special, and more privileged than the rest.
entities.name: Heart of a Nation

desc: In a Europe increasingly torn apart by bloody and fanatical religious wars, Transylvania has bravely issued the Edict of Torda, the first law of universal religious tolerance in the Western world. By allowing Catholics, Lutherans, Calvinists, and Unitarians to coexist within a single legal framework, we have prevented the internal social collapse and civil strife seen throughout the Holy Roman Empire. This unprecedented religious peace makes our principality a safe haven for displaced scholars, scientists, and merchants, rapidly accelerating our adoption of modern administrative reforms and diverse cultural influences. Tolerance has become our greatest strategic asset.
entities.name: The Edict of Torda

desc: We have established world-class scientific institutions to oversee the intensive extraction of gold, silver, and salt from the multiple mountain ranges of our nation. By applying the latest mineralogical and chemical techniques, we have turned Transylvania into the primary treasury of the region. This industrial focus has created a new class of professional engineers and technocrats who manage the state's resources with scientific precision, ensuring long-term economic stability.
entities.name: The National Mining Academy

desc: While Transylvania has remained part of the Hungarian Kingdom, the local Romanian, Saxon, and Hungarian nobles have all maintained a unique degree of regional autonomy under their own Voivode, and lived in peace. This shared governance has allowed everyone to preserve their distinct faiths and customs despite their apparent differences. This internal collaboration has ensured a certain degree of internal peace and multiculturalism in the Carpathian interior.
entities.name: The Transylvanian Autonomy

desc: In the bustling cities of the Carpathian arc, merchants from our main cultural groups have begun to organize themselves into trade guilds and fraternities, often in competition or cooperation with the others. This is urbanizing a segment of the population, creating a middle class who funds schools and prints books. This economic rise will allow our nation to move beyond the village and into the marketplace of ideas and global commerce.
entities.name: The Transylvanian Trade Guilds

desc: As the age of gunpowder reaches its peak, we have adopted a unique school of military architecture that adapts the latest Italian and French ''Trace Italienne'' designs to the rugged, limestone geography of the Carpathian interior. Our major administrative centers have been refortified with low-profile, angled bastions capable of absorbing heavy siege artillery fire. Unlike the massive stone walls of the past, these modern earth-and-brick works are designed for active defense, featuring interlocking fields of fire for the principality's growing artillery corps. This defensive doctrine ensures that any invading army is bled dry in a series of prolonged, costly sieges before they can ever threaten the state's heartland.
entities.name: The Bastion Synthesis

desc: In response to threats of peasant revolts, our higher classes have formed the 'Union of the Three Nations'. This complex and rigid legal framework largely excludes the commoner majority, but creates a highly stable, fortified, and loyal administrative core for the region. This internal unity provides the crown with a reliable base of professional urban and feudal soldiers.
entities.name: Unio Trium Nationum

desc: As trade routes were revived and expanded during the Middle Ages, new mercantile practices began to appear. One such were trade fairs, large-scale events held annually in towns and cities where merchants and traders from different places could meet and broker deals.
entities.name: Trade Fairs

desc: Lucrative trade routes have crossed our territories since ancient times. Our people are used to interacting with long caravan trains of merchants trading in goods from lands far away.
entities.name: Trade Caravans

desc: With clever techniques, we can easily make our controlled markets more attractive to foreign merchants, increasing the amount of money we earn in the process.
entities.name: Emporiums

desc: It has always been plain that money makes the world go 'round. With desirable new products constantly being discovered in distant lands, trade companies that specialize in distributing them are sure to reap enormous profits.
entities.name: Trade Companies

desc: With the recent increase in trade to and from faraway lands, our envoys have started joining trade expeditions to establish diplomatic contacts with countries that were previously out of our reach.
entities.name: Trade Envoys

desc: At those key choke points where trade supremacy could go one way or another, edging out the regional competition is crucial to expanding our trade income.
entities.name: Trade Manipulation

desc: Our position along the English Channel allows us to flourish as a commercial gateway. By investing in our port towns and merchant infrastructure, we can dominate regional trade while minimizing the cost of overseas operations.
entities.name: Channel Trade Ports

desc: As our economy grows, new opportunities arise. Whereas before short-distance trade routes were very profitable, longer-distance routes have recently started to bring in more money. Our merchant vessels are now sailing farther away for the best offers.
entities.name: Distant Markets

desc: We have developed larger ships that require a smaller crew to sail, and which can travel farther without needing to stop. This should greatly increase the range of our trade efforts as a result.
entities.name: Improved Trade Ships

desc: Merchants rarely stay still in one place, always trying to find the most profitable trades. Their constant coming and going is a common sight in our lands, and over time they have beaten their own paths to shorten the journey to their destinations.
entities.name: Merchant Trails

desc: The numerous trade ships coming in and out of our waters have familiarized us with many distant realms. By establishing permanent trading embassies with these far-off places, we can transform casual commerce into formal relationships.
entities.name: Trading Embassies

desc: A vital point across our trade network, the Trading Hub constitutes a great place to sell and purchase many exotic and local goods.
entities.name: Trading Hub

desc: Our country has been a crossroads of trade since ancient times. Our proximity to India and China has allowed trade to flow through our lands, and with it relationships and interactions with the many different countries around us.
entities.name: Trading Links

desc: It is always tempting to be a little late paying soldiers of fortune — after all, you never know what sudden expenses might come along. But we will ''not do that''; we shall pay our mercenaries exactly on time, and mercenary captains will know this and remember this.
entities.name: Tradition of Payment

desc: The Training Fields can be built in [Rural Location] as another source of [
entities.name: Training Fields

desc: Genghis Khān made the world tremble with his conquests, and we will do the same. The world will learn to fear the sound of galloping hoofbeats as our riders approach!
entities.name: Trampling Horde

desc: Our traders frequently bring back fascinating things from the courts of North Africa. Perhaps they could find and bring back yet more fascinating trinkets?
entities.name: Trans-Sahara Trade

desc: The caravans of the great Saharan routes trade Salt and other goods from North Africa for Slaves and Gold from the Sub-Saharan kingdoms. Through these valuable avenues of coin, we will build our great legacy.
entities.name: Trans-Saharan Trade

desc: The great Byzantine Empire, under the rule of our forefathers, was truly something to behold. Deceit and treachery may have toppled their regime, but Byzantium has risen like the phoenix to reclaim its former glory, and now no one shall doubt our authority!
entities.name: Byzantine Birthright

desc: We inherit some of the bureaucracy of our former empire, allowing us to maintain order and governance despite our reduced circumstances.
entities.name: Empire in Exile

desc: The Komnenos dynasty may have been expelled from the Byzantine throne long ago, but its glory never faded. Members of our lineage are still shown the appropriate deference, and this respect and admiration stretches far beyond our borders.
entities.name: Grand Komnenoi

desc: Since ancient times, Greek has been the language of education and science. When our ancestors came here, they not only brought their determination, but also their culture and native tongue. As such, the Greek tradition of learning is very much alive in our country.
entities.name: Greek Stronghold

desc: Some remarkable women have emerged from along the Komnenos, and many among the rulers of Europe and even the infidels have sought their hands in matrimony. Our line is well-respected, and our princesses doubly so, for they are what allow foreign countries to claim legitimacy through our line, and us to maintain influence in foreign courts.
entities.name: Komnenoi Princesses

desc: Let nobody forget that we are the descendants of the Komnenos that ruled over the Byzantine Empire. Although we now rule a different state, the legacy and prestige of our dynasty remains undeniable.
entities.name: Komnenos Legacy

desc: Isaakios Angelos, who deposed our line centuries ago, was himself deposed and blinded. On the pretense of putting the blind old fool back on the throne, the Venetian troops then sacked Constantinople. If there is something to learn from this incident, it is that treason and deceit are ubiquitous in the struggle for power, but they can also safeguard victory.
entities.name: Lessons of the Fourth Crusade

desc: Much as the Alps separate the French and Italian, the Pontic Mountains separate our last Greek holdout in Anatolia from the Turkic invaders who have seized the Anatolian Plateau. Pontus has always been more Greek than the rest of Anatolia; perhaps the legacy of the great Mithridates will inspire our warriors and strike as much fear into the Turks as he did the Romans?
entities.name: Pontic Mountains

desc: Our land is like our home; its forests, our garden. We know every bit of it better than anyone. Every path and every trail that crosses it is known to us, and we will make use of that knowledge if any dare to invade us.
entities.name: Pontic Trail Mastery

desc: The Laz have inhabited these lands for centuries. While our Empire was forged by Greek people, many Laz nonetheless remain within our borders. This has led to some of our enemies calling us Princes of the Laz in mockery, regarding us as inferiors. However, no matter what they say, it does not diminish our heritage, and we shall wear the title proudly.
entities.name: Princes of the Laz

desc: Kingdoms are conquered not only by the sword. By forging marriage alliances with surrounding nations, we create opportunities to inherit their thrones — and, at the very least, extend stronger influence over them.
entities.name: Strategic Marriages

desc: Even when it was called Trapezous in the mists of antiquity, our nation was the point where the land route across Asia meets the sea route leading to the Mediterranean. We grew famous as the terminal point for the great Silk Road, the wealth of China and India passing through our lands on its way to Europe. Since our nation still lies in this crucial location, there is no reason for us not to continue and encourage this steady flow of intercontinental trade.
entities.name: Terminus of the Silk Road

desc: Banished from our country, and yet our line survived. Forced to live in a mountainous wasteland surrounded by enemies, and yet our people thrived. We are a resourceful people, determined to make the most of what we have and to best whatever situation we encounter.
entities.name: Trapezuntine Endurance

desc: It is our faith that saves the souls of our people, and our clergy are the ones who ensure their salvation. What,  then, are our monasteries, if not the source and origin of such salvation?
entities.name: Trapezuntine Monasteries

desc: The Tree of Peace is the legacy of the Great Peacemaker, and is a symbol of our commitment to unity among the different tribes, as well as a representation of the chiefs themselves.
entities.name: Tree of Peace

desc: Our territory is both home to many urban areas and castles of many imperial knights. Balancing them and their often opposing interests is no easy task. Only if they cooperate with us and the cathedral chapter, we can ensure the functionality of our government.
entities.name: Balance the Landstände

desc: As time progresses, so does our understanding of our culture and identity. We no longer have to fear neighboring tribes; we have tamed the wilderness and have become its master. Now it is time to embrace who we are as a people.
entities.name: Tribal Cultural Identity

desc: Our people do not permanently occupy out lands. Instead, we travel freely, as fate and our people's needs dictate.
entities.name: Tribal Migration

desc: The time has come to discard our old ways and embrace a position in the larger world. No longer seen as a mere tribe, we shall officially become a country, one that represents and defends our people and the way we live.
entities.name: Tribal Modernization

desc: The religious values of our tribe dictate not only how we live, but how we treat those who do not share our beliefs and traditions, both within and outside of our territory.
entities.name: Tribal Religious Values

desc: A system of subjugated local warlords and other rulers who send us regular gifts of allegiance in recognition of our overlordship. To refine and centralize this system would help us tighten our grip and squeeze more out of them.
entities.name: Tributary System

desc: Strengthen our income by establishing a formalized system of yearly tribute from our vassals.
entities.name: Tribute System

desc: Utilizing the unique hydrology of the Trebišnjica river (the world's longest sinking river), the state will build a series of stone aqueducts and mills. This will allow for intensive agriculture even in the dry summer months, making the state self-sufficient in grain and able to withstand long maritime blockades.
entities.name: The Aqueducts of Popovo Polje

desc: The state will introduce a written constitution that will limit the power of the ruler and grant rights to the 'Assembly of Lords and Citizens'. This will be one of the first liberal documents in the Balkans, intended to prevent internal revolution and present Travunja as a 'Civilized State' to the great powers of Europe, ensuring our continued sovereignty.
entities.name: The Constitution of Trebinje

desc: To counter the expansion of our enemies, the state will rebuild the fortress of Klobuk into a modern citadel. We will introduce a system of 'Signal Fires' across the ''Popovo Polje'', allowing the garrison at Trebinje to alert the entire hinterland of an invasion within hours. This will create a zone of control that will make the region impossible to bypass.
entities.name: The Defensive Network of Klobuk

desc: Following the model of Roman engineering, the local lords will invest in massive stone bridges to ensure that the 'Silver Road' from the interior never closes during winter floods. This investment in infrastructure will allow for the year-round movement of heavy trade caravans between the mountains and the coastal towns.
entities.name: The Trebišnjica Bridges

desc: As the great Mediterranean wars intensify, the Travunjan state will leverage its unique relationship with the Jewish and Ragusan merchant families (the ''Zudiosca'') to build a sophisticated espionage ring. Because these traders move freely between the mountain interior and the Adriatic ports, they provide the Travunjan commanders with real-time troop movements of foreign armies. This 'Invisible Guard' will allow the local army to always strike at the enemy's weakest point, effectively nullifying the numbers of any invading power.
entities.name: The Zudiosca Network

desc: Under previous rulers, the traditional Slavic ''Župa'' (district) of Travunja was reorganized to better collect the ''Soj'' (land tax). The ruler appointed ''Kephale'' (heads) to oversee the Trebišnjica Valley, ensuring that the wealth from the fertile plains reached the central treasury. This proto-bureaucracy allowed our past rulers to fund their wars by squeezing wealth from the productive agricultural output of the hinterlands. We shall continue with this tradition.
entities.name: Župa Administrative Reform

desc: In our quest to shore up our border defenses, it has become apparent that we must create a system of recruitment centered around local soldiers and stalwarts. These fighters will be a valuable addition to our military capabilities, and shall be kept separate from the ''Wèi Suǒ'' system.
entities.name: Tǔ Bīng

desc: We will reform old and stagnant traditions, plant tulips in all gardens, and usher in a new golden age of commerce and connection.
entities.name: Tulip Period

desc: From their strongholds in Tunis and La Goulette, our corsairs dominate the Mediterranean. With swift galleys and the power of state sponsorship behind them, they strike fear into foreign merchants and bolster our naval strength with ruthless efficiency.
entities.name: Tunisian Corsairs

desc: Although the Borjigin dynasty has a Mongolian origin, the territories conquered by Genghis Khān in Central Asia were mainly hose of Turkic populations. As a result, a distinct blended culture emerged between those two groups.
entities.name: Turco-Mongol Tradition

desc: Persia has always been the undeniable center of culture and language in the region, influencing the different Turkic peoples that have been around for centuries. We will embrace this blend of cultures to create our own unique tradition.
entities.name: Turco-Persian Tradition

desc: We hail from the steppes. The wind, the hardships, and the thrill of battle will always be in our blood, and we must never forget them.
entities.name: Turkic Traditions

desc: We shall commission the ''Catasto'' — the most comprehensive survey of wealth and property undertaken by any government in medieval Europe, mapping the taxable assets of every citizen and household from the wealthiest merchant to the humblest artisan. By laying bare the full extent of our fiscal base, the Catasto allows us to distribute the burden of taxation with unprecedented fairness, replacing the factional manipulation of the old system with transparent and enforceable assessments. This reform earns the trust of our subjects, eases the cost of governing, and establishes a standard of administrative precision that future rulers of Tuscany will build upon.
entities.name: Il Catasto Fiorentino

desc: The ''Contado'' — the ring of rural territory surrounding each of our cities — has long been the foundation of Tuscan wealth and power, its villages, castles, and farmlands bound by law and custom to answer to the urban lord within the walls. By formalizing our jurisdiction over the countryside, we transform scattered feudal obligations into a coherent system of agricultural surplus, military manpower, and direct revenue. This mastery of the contado anchors our legitimacy among the landed classes and extends our reach into every corner of the land we claim to rule.
entities.name: Il Contado

desc: The rational spirit of the Enlightenment has taken deep root in our cities, where thinkers and reformers challenge superstition, codify the law, and redesign our institutions from the ground up. Our rulers, schooled in the new philosophy, regard the welfare of their subjects as both a moral duty and a measure of good government. This commitment to reason and reform is transforming our streets, our courts, and our academies into models for the modern world.
entities.name: Tuscan Enlightenment

desc: Our cities have given rise to learned societies dedicated to the purification of language, the pursuit of knowledge, and the cultivation of civic virtue. From the philological investigations of our literary scholars to the natural philosophy of our scientists, these academies gather the finest minds of the age and sharpen the wit of our administrators. This tradition of organized inquiry is already raising the quality of our governance and the ambition of our institutions.
entities.name: Tuscan Literary Academies

desc: Across the great trading cities of the continent, the name of our merchants is known wherever bills of exchange are signed and goods are weighed. From the wool markets of England to the spice routes of the Levant, our trading houses extend our reach far beyond our borders, wielding an influence that no army could match. This web of commerce and credit ensures our voice is heard in the courts of distant kings.
entities.name: Tuscan Merchant Houses

desc: Our ruler governs Tuscany by the principles of the ''Physiocrates'', which state that land and agriculture are the true sources of all wealth. We will abolish serfdom and guild monopolies, work to free the grain trade from state controls, and will be reorganizing taxation around soil productivity rather than the privileges of merchants and nobles. This same spirit of rational governance is restructuring our commercial culture, dismantling the internal barriers that previously restricted the movement of goods and opening our markets to trade that guild charters had long excluded. This comprehensive reform of land and commerce is transforming Tuscany into a model of Enlightened administration, an experiment in rational governance that observers across Europe come to study and imitate.
entities.name: Tuscan Physiocratic Reforms

desc: Across the fertile hills and valleys of our lands, the ancient partnership between landowner and sharecropper ensures that fields are worked with care and harvests shared in good faith. The ''Mezzadria'' is more than an agricultural arrangement — it is a social covenant that sustains both the peasantry and the merchant class who depend on the contado's output. This bond between city and countryside is the foundation upon which our prosperity rests.
entities.name: The Mezzadria

desc: Our commissioning of the ''Uffizi'' as the administrative heart of our new Grand Duchy creates not merely a seat of government, but a stage for our power — its long corridor soon to be lined with antiquities, sculptures, and canvases that announce our ruler's dynasty's mastery of both statecraft and beauty. Across the city, we are establishing a secret workshop in the Palazzo Vecchio, where alchemists and craftsmen perfect a soft-paste porcelain — the first produced in Europe, rivalling the precious wares imported at great expense from China. These twin achievements of administration and artisanal ambition mark the apex of our patronage, announcing to every court in Christendom that Tuscany under the Grand Dukes is as much a center of refinement as of power.
entities.name: Uffizi

desc: Titles granted to warlords and local strongmen, these administrative positions are used to quell unrest and keep the rural populace under central control.
entities.name: Tǔsī Titles

desc: Due to the size of our realm, our jurisdiction falls under two distinct frameworks: To the north lies the core of our territories, proudly embracing our cultural traditions and social mores. However, our southern and eastern regions often diverge to a certain degree from our central norms. To respect such diversity will strengthen our nation as well as our position on the geopolitical stage.
entities.name: Two Realms

desc: A particular struggle of our unified country is governing both sides of the Strait of Messina. Since our ruler can only be present on one side at a time, the other will have to be given to a vicar, ruling in our name. We must be sure to appoint only the most capable and trustworthy people to this vital role to prevent corruption.
entities.name: Capable Vicars

desc: The Noble Families of both Sicilies exert much power in our stead. By granting them prestigious yet meaningless roles at court, we will ensure their loyalty and guarantee stable rule over our countryside.
entities.name: Loyalty of the Noble Families

desc: Expanding our territories within Italy is a difficult task, navigating a treacherous web of alliances and risking the anger of the Pope himself. Therefore, we should look overseas, where potential riches await us in the lands of northern Africa and Greece.
entities.name: Overseas Ambitions

desc: Our coastline is vast, and vulnerable to raids by pirates hunting for slaves. We need to establish a navy to patrol, protect, and eventually defeat this vile threat to our people.
entities.name: Increase Maritime Patrols

desc: Previous rulers put too much focus on particular areas of our country. If we want to retain control of both Sicilies, we will have to invest equally and fairly in both parts. One step towards this goal is attracting people to settle in previously neglected areas.
entities.name: Attract new People

desc: The territories which constitute our land have suffered revolts due to unjust applications of laws. In order to prevent these occurrences in the future, we should standardize our legal code and ensure our laws are applied fairly. This will surely prevent any uprising from spiraling into chaos.
entities.name: Unified Legal Code

desc: The Uç Bey is an [Army Based Country] that serves as a frontier lord under strong Turkic leadership. Tasked with defending borders, leading raids, and expanding territories, these semi-autonomous leaders command loyal Ġuzāt warriors driven by religious fervor, plunder, and land grants, making them crucial to frontier stability and expansion. They can only be created through the Create Uç Bey [
], and they get the Uç Bey Government [

] and Always Allow Army Levies, while having greatly reduced payment obligations compared to a normal Vassal but costing increased [Diplomatic Capacity] and giving their overlord more Monthly Towards Decentralization.
entities.name: Uç Bey

desc: We have been appointed ''Shugo'' of both Kōzuke and Tango Provinces. Their plentiful lands are the perfect starting point for our expansion.
entities.name: Double Shugo

desc: Our clan has fostered such an extraordinary spirit of courage and justice that it intimidates our opponents on the battlefield. We will declare the strength of our leaders to all the world, and everyone will quake with terror at the thought of the Dragon of Echigo!
entities.name: Dragon of Echigo

desc: Although we have been granted territory in both eastern and western Japan, it is in the east where we will truly be able to flourish. Our territories there are rich, and we can attract many skilled local warriors to fight for our cause.
entities.name: Eastern Power

desc: Our family descends from the prestigious line of the Fujiwara, and we also have strong ties to the Ashikaga, as the mother of Ashikaga Takauji was a member of our clan. These dynastic ties will prove invaluable for our prosperity.
entities.name: Strong Dynastic Ties

desc: Ukraine, or the 'borderlands' in slavic language, is one of the most fertile regions in Europe. The lands along both banks of the great rivers are renowned for their rich black soil, yielding abundant harvests of grain, legumes, and fiber crops. Whoever holds these territories commands a significant agricultural advantage, supplying their realm's granaries and the markets of Europe.
entities.name: Ukrainian Farmlands

desc: The tradition passed down to us by Jesus Christ and the apostles is consistent, without any changes, additions, or subtractions whatsoever. Our faith is undeniable in its truths, and what is fundamentally true about this world cannot be changed by mortal hands.
entities.name: Unchanging Tradition

desc: It cannot be denied that Islam has spread to many different cultures and peoples since its emergence in Arabia. As long as they believe in Allāh, any person should be able to fight in His name, regardless of their origin.
entities.name: Unified Armies

desc: For much of our history the priesthood responsible for sacred lands and temple revenues has functioned in a decentralized manner. Yet recent developments in foreign religious institutions have introduced new ideas of organization and central authority. These influences now encourage the unification and coordination of our own priestly hierarchy.
entities.name: Unify the Priestly Class

desc: The relative isolation of our patriarchates have resulted in the development of unique architectural styles for our holy places. Although other Christian denominations may be more prominent, our captivating architecture is an inspiration to the faithful.
entities.name: Unique Architecture

desc: Since the birth of our nation, the Jurchen people have been unified and divided into multiple tribes and alliances, and not always friendly ones. This dynamic has been constant for as long as we can remember — as has the urge to unify all our tribes under a single banner. The time has come to satisfy this long-cherished desire!
entities.name: Unite the Tribes

desc: No matter our situation, we must ensure the unity of our faith. Only if our clergy is aligned, and no discord exists between factions of the faithful, will they be able to focus on their primary function of guiding and aiding our population.
entities.name: A United Faith

desc: A center of thought and innovation, the University is home to bright minds of scientists and men of letters alike, all eager to promote growth and literacy.
entities.name: University

desc: Founded in 1224 by Emperor Frederick II, the University of Naples is one of Italy's oldest public institutions. Embracing a secular ethos, it has provided generations of students with a comprehensive education and contributed to intellectual advancements across various fields.
entities.name: The University of Naples

desc: Archers support our footmen with ranged fire, allowing them to advance towards enemy lines when attacking and also helping them better protect their position when defending.
entities.name: Archers

desc: The Baltic Sea can be a dangerous place to navigate with warships. Its treacherous shallow waters require ships to operate with a small draft, otherwise risking loss of navigation and effectiveness. The Archipelago Frigate, a sailing ships equipped with oars, is well suited for the waters of the Baltic and will grant an edge in swiftness and lethality to the navy.
entities.name: Archipelago Frigate

desc: Horsemen who are more heavily armored, usually with some form of mail or full plate, to charge headlong into enemy ranks.
entities.name: Armored Horsemen

desc: A pike-and-shot formation consisting of a core of troops armed with firearms and protected by a phalanx of armored pikemen, the Arquebusiers are a formidable unit that cannot be easily countered.
entities.name: Arquebusiers

desc: Serving as larger variants of the Sekibune ships, the Atakebune is able to staff a larger crew than before. Sometimes equipped with iron or copper plates mounted on the hull, they improve on the survivability of the previous types as well.
entities.name: Atakebune

desc: The generalization of standing armies in the Reformation is further developing the supply needs of their soldiers, the use of a Baggage Train that follows the advance of the armies becoming commonplace.
entities.name: Baggage Train

desc: The Bǎochuán is a large vessel designed to transport goods and protect the trade on sea. They are capable of long distance voyages, bringing treasure and tribute from far away shores to our lands.
entities.name: Bǎochuán

desc: The Barque was a small sailing ship, originally used for trade. Adapting these for warfare provided a smaller and faster alternative to the larger carracks.
entities.name: Barque

desc: The Bomb Ketch is a specialized light ship to carry out shore bombardments. Sacrificing most of their cannons in exchange for mortars able to carry out heavy bombardment of stationary targets along the shoreline, these vessels can trivialize the siege of coastal fortifications.
entities.name: Bomb Ketch

desc: The brig was a small ship used for trade or war, characterized by having two square-rigged masts. When used for war, they were small vessels with 10 to 18 guns, but it was their speed and maneuverability what made them valuable assets. Their full square rigging also made them more suited when traveling along trade winds, when they would sail downwind for long periods of time.
entities.name: Brig

desc: The Late Medieval Cataphracts are mail-clad riders and horses alike, thundering into battle behind long lances and dense shields. Their shock charges and iron discipline are a frightening sight for our foes.
entities.name: Late Medieval Cataphracts

desc: These Reformed Cataphracts blend old Imperial drills with newer tactics, combining lances with bows and sidearms. They fight as a flexible heavy cavalry corps, able to harass at range and then finish off their foes in close combat.
entities.name: Reformed Cataphracts

desc: The Heavy Cataphracts ride in layered armor that deflects most missiles and blades. Organized into wedges of elite fighters, they break enemy lines with repeated charges that few formations can withstand.
entities.name: Heavy Cataphracts

desc: Chosen from the finest lancers, the Guard Cataphracts serve as the mounted guard of the throne and our capital. Their presence in every battle is both a weapon and a symbol, rallying our troops and terrifying our foes.
entities.name: Guard Cataphracts

desc: The Imperial Cataphracts are the culmination of centuries of cavalry tradition: armored veterans, superbly mounted and drilled to perfection. They serve as the Emperor's personal guard, able to decide campaigns with a single, well-timed charge.
entities.name: Imperial Cataphracts

desc: A large and heavily armed ship, propelled by oars and two or even three sails, the Cakradonya will dominate the seas of Indonesia.
entities.name: Cakradonya

desc: The caravel was a small, very maneuverable ship which could sail with high precision on long discovery journeys. Although designs varied, a caravel had a foresail, a square mainsail and a lateen mizzen. Its smaller size limited the number of guns onboard, but it also meant that this light ship could explore shallow coastal waters and estuaries. Vasco Da Gama, Cabot, Columbus and Magellan used caravels during their late 15th century and early 16th century voyages.
entities.name: Caravel

desc: The design of the carrack, a late medieval ship, combined the features of Germanic longships and Arabic merchantmen. It was less maneuverable than the caravel, but because of its larger size, it could carry provisions for long voyages, cargo for trade, and guns for self-defense. Some carracks such as the English vessel 'Henri Grâce à Dieu' weighed more than 1,000 tons, had large fore and aft castles, and could be considered as the greatest warships of their time.
entities.name: Carrack

desc: Cavalrymen are light cavalry, sometimes armed with ranged weapons, used to attack enemy lines, although they may sometimes be ready to charge into close combat.
entities.name: Cavalrymen

desc: The 16th century did not only see improvements in artillery maneuverability but also in the attempts at standardizing the size and weight of artillery pieces.
entities.name: Chambered Cannon

desc: The cog was a small ship widely used in medieval Europe. Characterized by having a single mast with a square sail, and constructed with overlapping planks, it was an evolution of the Viking merchant ships. Their construction made them more suitable for navigating the North Atlantic than the Mediterranean vessels, while their simpler rigging required fewer people to operate. It was used extensively by the Hanseatic League until eventually replaced by the hulk.
entities.name: Cog

desc: Crossbowmen are a type of ranged fire unit that harness the increased firepower of crossbows, a much more powerful, albeit slow-reloading, projectile weapon.
entities.name: Crossbowmen

desc: Keeping up with the changing times, Cuirassiers are heavy cavalry that have discarded lances in favor of pistols and sabers as their primary weapon.
entities.name: Cuirassiers

desc: A common trading ship in the Indian Ocean, the Dhow is a capable vessel for trading in the region, despite its small hull size.
entities.name: Dhow

desc: The arquebus is the evolution of the handgonne, making it a more reliable type of gunpowder weapon as it is easier and faster to reload, making it ideal for deploying larger gunpowder fire units.
entities.name: Early Arquebusiers

desc: The early carrack was the first European vessel that could sail on the high seas of the Atlantic Ocean. The design of this late medieval ship combined the features of Germanic longships and Arabic merchantmen. It was less maneuverable than the caravel, but because of its larger size, it could carry provisions for long voyages, cargo for trade, and guns for self-defense.
entities.name: Early Carrack

desc: The powerful martial longbow, originally deployed with great impact against armored English knights in the Welsh valleys, has been adopted into the military doctrine on either side of the border.
entities.name: Warbows

desc: The Eastindiaman was a general term for all ships operating for any of the East India Trading Companies. Being able to carry both passengers and goods, they were built at first to carry as much as possible. They were still armed to defend themselves against pirates, so they could also participate in war engagement, but trade was always their main function.
entities.name: East-Indiaman

desc: The Falconet is a light cannon developed in the 15th century as an evolution of the similar falcon, being more mobile while firing smaller caliber shots.
entities.name: Falconet

desc: A Feudal Levies is formed by peasants that are drafted in times of war as part of their duty towards their feudal lord, and have some military training. These levies are to eventually be replaced by professional armies.
entities.name: Feudal Levies

desc: The flintlock musket has replaced the matchlock arquebus as the primary infantry weapon, providing greater and more accurate firepower while being easier to use and maintain.
entities.name: Flintlock Levy

desc: A cargo ship developed in the Netherlands in the 16th century, it was built to maximize cargo space and crew efficiency. And it became one of the most commonly used ships in the 16th and 17th centuries. The standard design wasn't armed but when needed it could be armed with cannons and serve as auxiliary vessels.
entities.name: Flute

desc: Artillery is devastating on the battlefield, but completely useless if the enemy does not enter its firing range. A Flying Battery has the capability of relocating itself to where it is most needed and quickly redeploy before any enemy's retaliation.
entities.name: Flying Battery

desc: The backbone of every army, footmen comprise the majority of our marching troops, eager to sustain a frontline and defend our home from prospecting invaders.
entities.name: Footmen

desc: As time passed, the frigate evolved. It became larger and heavily armed, sometimes with two gun decks. The frigate's combination of speed and firepower meant that it could outrun any ship with more guns and outgun any faster ships. The fleet built by the Commonwealth of England in the 1650s consisted almost exclusively of frigates.
entities.name: Frigate

desc: Fusiliers are the backbone of our armies, armed with a modern ranged rifle and a bayonet that can be attached to it and enables the possibility of massed charges into enemy ranks.
entities.name: Fusiliers

desc: A fast variant of a galley, the Galiot is well suited for the waters of the Mediterranean Sea, being able to navigate both shallow and deep sea.
entities.name: Galiot

desc: The galleass was an adaptation of the large merchant galley to counter the increasing use of man-of-war. Larger than the galley, the galleass had about 32 oar pairs, each oar manned by up to five men. As an answer to the men-of-war's armament and higher sides, the galleass had forecastles and aftcastles and gun decks above the rowers. This extra weight meant that they also had to rely more on sails, and were slower and less maneuverable compared to galleys. Like the galley, the galleass went out of regular use with the introduction of more advanced oceangoing men-of-war, but remained useful in shallow waters until the 18th century.
entities.name: Galleass

desc: A large, usually three-masted sailing ship originally designed as a warship but later on used primarily for trade and commerce.
entities.name: Galleon

desc: Gallop Cavalry is a shock unit that charges the enemy with long cavalry sabers, protected with a certain degree of armor, which is a good balance between mobility and forcefulness.
entities.name: Gallop Cavalry

desc: Heavy infantry fitted with mail and wielding two-handed axes, the fearsome Gallowglass descend from Norse sea raiders who settled along the Atlantic coast.
entities.name: Gallowglass

desc: Evolved from earlier units equipped with explosives, these Grenadiers serve as elite vanguards for our armies. While the grenades from which their name comes are no longer their sole focus, their superior training makes them excellent assault troops.
entities.name: Grenadiers

desc: Halberdiers are units of soldiers that wield polearms, such as halberds, which are used for close combat, both offensively and defensively.
entities.name: Halberdiers

desc: Handgonners wield a new type of gunpowder-filled weapon that fires deadly lead shells, wreaking havoc on enemy lines, though they need to be fully protected as their handgonnes are very slow to reload.
entities.name: Handgonners

desc: A heavier type of cavalry, fully armored and trained for shock charges, thanks to its heavy armor and armament, which should lead to the disruption of the enemy line.
entities.name: Heavy Cavalrymen

desc: The heavy frigate was introduced by the British in the 18th century as a larger variant of the frigate in terms of both size and power of its guns. Having more and bigger guns meant an increase in their firepower and resulted in ships of individually greater force. Heavy frigates became the standard frigates during the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
entities.name: Heavy Frigate

desc: Heavy Lancers are the heaviest type of shock cavalry possible, and feature fully armored armor and the finest shock lances. Their charges are designed to completely disrupt the enemy formation, and they are also much more protected from enemy fire at range.
entities.name: Heavy Lancers

desc: Lightly-armored fighters mounted upon swift horses, bands of Horsemen have the mobility to harass, charge, and pursue.
entities.name: Horsemen

desc: It is believed modern howitzers have their name from the Houfnice artillery developed by the Hussites in the 15th century. These short-barreled guns were mounted on wagons and used on the field of battle to fire balls and canisters in support of the infantry.
entities.name: Houfnice

desc: The hulk was a type of European ship, the predecessor of the carrack and caravel, that originated in the Low Countries as a river boat, and was used predominantly as a cargo vessel, although it could be also used in war. It was constructed with a single mast with a square sail, and with a castle on both ends of the ship. Capable of rivaling the cog's carrying capacity, the hulk was the main trade ship used by the Hanseatic League.
entities.name: Hulk

desc: Hunters are light infantry designed to attack enemy formations from long range as they approach, attempting to disorganize them and make their own firepower much less effective.
entities.name: Hunters

desc: The hussars were originally light cavalry troops originating in Central Europe that were used for scouting, but with the decline of the old feudal army they were switched over to professional regiments.
entities.name: Hussars

desc: Strong cavalry armed with a lance, these shock troops are meant to break through enemy lines and devastate our foes' forces.
entities.name: Lancers

desc: A blend of old and new, these Late Gallowglass are heavily-armored troops outfitted with a medley of modern weapons such as arquebus guns to complement their traditional greatswords and axes.
entities.name: Late Gallowglass

desc: Small innovations in equipment and organization result in continuous devastating volleys that shatter all but the most heavily armored formations.
entities.name: Reformed Longbowmen

desc: The Early Legionaries uphold the oldest traditions of drill and discipline. Spears, broad shields, and firm cohesion let them stand fast even as the battle twists around them.
entities.name: Early Legionaries

desc: Legionaries trained in the refined arts of close combat, carrying throwing spears and short swords. Their strength lies in steady formations and a military culture of relentless practice.
entities.name: Legionaries

desc: The Reformed Legionaries are hardened infantrymen, equipped with the best armor and weapons, who form the core of our armies.
entities.name: Reformed Legionaries

desc: The Heavy Legionaries are elite infantrymen, equipped with the finest armor and weapons. Like the heavy armored legions of ancient Rome, these troops will be the hammer with which we will smite our enemies.
entities.name: Heavy Legionaries

desc: The Guard Legionaries embody the highest standard of soldiering within the legions. Selected from the finest cohorts, they are trusted with critical missions and the protection of the state's highest institutions.
entities.name: Guard Legionaries

desc: These Imperial Legionaries stand at the apex of centuries of military evolution. Masters of equipment and doctrine alike, they serve the lifeguard whose presence alone can steady wavering lines.
entities.name: Imperial Legionaries

desc: Light Dragoons are a type of light cavalry that can move, dismount, and shoot at the enemy with the rifles they carry, but are also armed with cavalry sabers, which allow them to charge the enemy if the opportunity arises.
entities.name: Light Dragoons

desc: Light Lancers are a type of light cavalry more focused on shock combat, as they use a charging lance, also wearing some degree of armor. However, they base their success on the battlefield on maintaining a high degree of mobility.
entities.name: Light Lancers

desc: A strict operation consisting of supply trains and an efficient bureaucracy, Logistics Corps represent the pinnacle of military organization during the Revolutions to support vast armies.
entities.name: Logistics Corps

desc: The ships of Ireland and the Highlands are most capable at projecting our presence over our coastal possessions, protecting merchant vessels and at the same time, serving as adequate warships in times of need.
entities.name: Long Fada

desc: An improved Long Fada, the Great Long Fada is a larger vessel with more oars and a bigger crew, able to carry out longer voyages and project more power over the seas.
entities.name: Great Long Fada

desc: The Longbowmen excel not only due to their powerful warbow but also their years of training on the archery fields.
entities.name: Longbowmen

desc: With roots back to the ancient ships of antiquity, the galley remained the prime choice for Mediterranean naval warfare until the 16th century. The galley was primarily propelled by oars, usually about 25 pairs manned by up to three men each. This meant that they were less dependent on wind gauges compared to sailing ships, and their maneuverability made them a feared adversary. Eventually, the galley went out of regular use with the introduction of more advanced oceangoing men-of-war, but remained useful in shallow waters until the 18th century.
entities.name: Mediterranean Galley

desc: The development of the matchlock arquebus makes it possible to arm large numbers of soldiers with gunpowder weapons on a scale that was not possible in the Middle Ages.
entities.name: Matchlock Levy

desc: Armored footmen outfitted with a medley of hand-to-hand weapons, Men-at-Arms are heavy melee infantry who can break through enemy formations.
entities.name: Men-at-Arms

desc: Merchantman is a type of ship used for commerce carrying goods or passengers. They would generally include some armament to protect themselves from pirates and privateers, especially if engaging in long travels, in which case they could even be heavily armed.
entities.name: Merchantman

desc: The musketeers are the elite fighting force of the royal household. Being a musketeer is a position of great prestige and only nobles with years of military service are allowed to join the company's ranks.
entities.name: Musketeers

desc: A Peasant Levy is formed by commoners summoned for military service by their Lord. The men are meant to bring their own equipment to battle, so the quality of newly created units can vary greatly.
entities.name: Peasant Levy

desc: Pikemen are footmen armed with pikes, allowing them to form dense formations that easily confront enemy cavalry charges, thus negating the power of cavalry on the battlefield.
entities.name: Pikemen

desc: With the increasing overseas trade, there was a need for a fast escort vessel to provide a safe journey. The Pinnace was developed for this. It was a smaller, leaner warship with one gun deck, and it provided protection from piracy in dangerous waters.
entities.name: Pinnace

desc: Pistoleers are light cavalrymen armed with pistols, a type of gunpowder weapon that is easier to carry and handle on horseback, but can also be used as a melee weapon, thanks to its heavy, reinforced grip.
entities.name: Pistoleers

desc: Adapting to the changing warfare, the Crusader Sergeants have adopted new tactics and refined weaponry. With these adaptions they will retain their status as the elite foot forces of the Military Orders, side by side with the Order Knights.
entities.name: Order Sergeants

desc: The gradual influence of continental-style warfare has led to better-equipped and more cohesive units of Gallowglass.
entities.name: Reformed Gallowglass

desc: From the second half of the 17th century the use of artillery on the battlefield became more widespread. The troops were now able to move their field guns with much more ease and speed.
entities.name: Royal Mortar

desc: Build from cider or fir wood, the Sekibune sacrifices a sturdy hull for increased speed and maneuverability.
entities.name: Sekibune

desc: Sharpshooters are a type of light infantry unit made up of the best marksmen, who use rifles with a longer range, making them better at skirmishing and disrupting enemy formations while maneuvering.
entities.name: Sharpshooters

desc: Some alterations to the standard Three-decker design, these ships will serve as flagships and the pride of the navy. While they are expensive to operate, these ships are potentially able to win combats on their own, due to their sturdier hull and superior firepower.
entities.name: First-Rate Ship of the Line

desc: The Supply Carts are the lifeline of any army wanting to venture outside home territories. They provided food to the men and the animals, extending the distance the army could travel before stopping to forage what can be very hostile lands.
entities.name: Supply Carts

desc: The transition from feudal levies to standing armies in the Discovery is allowing longer campaigns, creating the need to supply those soldiers for longer periods. That comes from the more organized Supply Convoy.
entities.name: Supply Convoy

desc: Three-deckers were warships that held three fully-armed decks with guns. Other guns could also be carried additionally on the forecastle or the quarterdeck, but only the batteries of the three main decks formed a continuous battery. Three-deckers were considered ships of the line, that is strong enough to participate in the line of battle.
entities.name: Three-decker

desc: Galleys of various forms have dominated the seas for millennia, and many remote shipwrights still construct them in the traditional ways. The skill of ship construction is passed down from generation to generation, although with little innovation.
entities.name: Traditional Galley

desc: Two-deckers were warships that held two fully-armed decks with guns. Other guns could also be carried additionally on the forecastle or the quarterdeck, but only the batteries of the two main decks formed a continuous battery.
entities.name: Two-decker

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Restored Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Pelekyphóroi Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Modernized Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Imperial Varangians

desc: Powerful warriors that originally hailed from the northern Viking lands, these select few ferocious soldiers make up the core of the royal guard. Armed with axes and shields, they have often been described as ''pelekyphóroi bárbaroi'', axe-wielding barbarians.
entities.name: Imperial Varangian Guard

desc: The growth in the size of armies during the Absolutism is making their logistics increasingly complex, making each army dependent on its own Wagon Train to maintain its combat performance in the field.
entities.name: Wagon Train

desc: Refocusing the design of the Galleon towards duties of warfare, the War Galleon will give us a great advantage in naval warfare.
entities.name: War Galleon

desc: War galleys are galleys used for war. They are long and shallow, propelled mainly by oars, although they generally also included some kind of sail. Used since ancient times, their presence was commonplace in the seas and oceans during the Middle Ages thanks to their higher maneuverability. Being used for boarding rather than long-range engagements, projectile weapons and guns were concentrated on the front of the ship, leaving the protection of the weak spots of the sides and the rear to the ability to out-maneuver their enemies.
entities.name: War Galley

desc: A two or three-masted small vessel widely used in the Mediterranean from the 16th century onwards.
entities.name: Xebec

desc: The potters and painters of our city have developed a tradition of tin-glazed ''maiolica'' whose vivid colors and intricate scenes are sought by collectors and courts across the continent. Our ceramic guilds guard and transmit their techniques across generations, ensuring that the quality which made our name endures. This craft industry exports our culture in every painted dish and decorated vessel that leaves our workshops.
entities.name: The Ceramics Guilds

desc: Our university has endured through changes of government and the upheavals of the ages, continuing to draw students and scholars to our city by the reputation of its teaching. The long tradition of ''learning'' established in our most glorious days has become a living institution that carries that spirit forward into a new era. This continuity of scholarship is our gift to the future and our connection to the greatness of our past.
entities.name: The Enlightened University

desc: The hilltops of our domain have been fortified over many generations, turning every elevated town into a position that would take a determined army weeks to reduce. Our soldiers learn their craft on these steep approaches and defend positions where a small garrison can hold off a much larger force. The ''Hill Fortress'' network of our territory is both our shield and the school in which our military tradition is trained.
entities.name: The Hill Fortresses

desc: Our court has been called the most perfectly ordered in all of Italy, and men of learning and artistic ambition travel great distances to take part in its life. The conversations, performances, and works of art we foster here have inspired accounts of what a ''Perfect Court'' might look like, and those accounts have spread our reputation far beyond our borders. This refinement of governance and culture is the greatest thing we have built.
entities.name: The Ideal Court

desc: We have nurtured a tradition of mathematical and philosophical inquiry that has made our city known throughout Europe for the precision of its thinkers. The ''Mathematical School'' of our court has produced translations, commentaries, and original works that advance the sciences and win us admiration from the finest universities. This commitment to learning opens our citizens' minds and sharpens our capacity to understand and shape the world.
entities.name: The Mathematical School

desc: We rule these hilltop towns and valleys as lords whose authority is ancient and whose right to govern has never been successfully challenged. Our people know that the ''Montefeltro'' have always defended their lands and their customs, and that loyalty has built a bond between lord and subject stronger than any decree. This seignory is not merely power over a territory but a compact that both sides have chosen to honor.
entities.name: The Montefeltro Seignory

desc: The new opportunities and security offered by life in our emerging cities are drawing more and more people off of rural farms and into cities, where they are eager to take up industrial jobs created by the new, modern factories.
entities.name: Urbanization

desc: As part of our efforts to modernize Prague, we will issue grants encouraging prominent figures to relocate their business to the capital while offering privileges to attract skilled and wealthy foreign immigrants. This influx of talent and capital will transform our Prague into a thriving, cosmopolitan metropolis.
entities.name: Urbanization Decrees

desc: ''...or abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press; or the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.''
entities.name: Bill of Rights

desc:
''We hold these truths to be self-evident, that all men are created equal.''

With this bold declaration, we shall break the chains of subjugation, and embraced our shared destiny!
entities.name: Declaration of Independence

desc: Elected assemblies emerged throughout the colonies, empowering landowners to govern themselves. The humble origins of liberty lie in the halls of these institutions.
entities.name: Empowered Assemblies

desc: In the wake of hardship, peace and unity have brought a rare moment of national harmony. The people flourish with optimism and order.
entities.name: Era of Good Feelings

desc: A wave of religious revival sweeps the land, challenging old authorities and stirring the moral conscience of a rising people.
entities.name: Great Awakening

desc: Bound together by shared peril and purpose, the early settlers drafted a pact of self-governance. Even in the wilderness, the seeds of society and compromise found soil.
entities.name: Mayflower Compact

desc: Treaties and diplomacy affirmed what our struggles have earned. Our place on the stage of diplomacy is no longer questioned, but respected.
entities.name: Recognized Sovereignty

desc: The Viking-like ''Ushkuynik'' pirates were once a useful tool to suppress our competitors. Unfortunately, we were forced to stop using them due to foreign intervention, mainly from Moscow. We should begin funding them again, and send these pirates to plunder farther shores — that will show everyone who the true masters of the North are!
entities.name: The Ushkuyniks

desc: Our genealogy shows that the ancestors of our clan were originally members of the Fujiwara family from Kyōto. This kinship to such an ancient and revered dynasty is very useful for making diplomatic connections to the Imperial Court and with the other clans.
entities.name: Fujiwara Descendants

desc: Shimotsuke was once the home of Nasu no Yoichi, who was famous for his abilities as an archer during the Genpei War. To this day, the warriors of Shimotsuke hold him in high regard; we are proud to be called 'the best archers in Kantō' and to carry on Nasu no Yoichi's legacy.
entities.name: Legacy of Nasu no Yoichi

desc: As one of the oldest clans in Kantō, we have a keen insight into regional politics, and have worked as a mediator between different factions on many occasions. This same comprehensive understanding of our home region allows us to expand our territory effectively without provoking others.
entities.name: Mediator of Kantō

desc: The Pope himself influences the election of our Prince-Bishop, challenging the traditional five-chapter election format that we had before. This is clear proof that our land has been divinely blessed!
entities.name: A Blessed Land

desc: Utrecht, often called the ''City of Churches'', is home to the iconic Dom Tower. The spiritual center of the Netherlands and the seat of the Bishopric of Utrecht, it has been a beacon of faith since antiquity.
entities.name: The City of Churches

desc: Given the growing influence of our neighbors, our nation's survival depends on our ability to find loyal, powerful allies who will support us in our times of need.
entities.name: Skilled Diplomats

desc: With the development of vaccines, physicians are able to provide the populace with immunity against deadly diseases. These vaccines are helping to reduce the spread of disease and prevent epidemics. By injecting a small amount of weakened or dead bacteria or virus into the body, the immune system is able to recognize and fight off the disease if it ever encounters it again.
entities.name: Vaccination

gate: is capital in south america or carribean

desc: By building extensive networks of canals and connecting the waterways of our homeland's valleys, we can greatly improve our irrigation techniques and the productivity of our farmlands.
entities.name: Inter-Valley Irrigation

desc: Our pantheon contains a remarkable variety of deities, each representing different virtues, crafts, and ideals. This diversity allows every individual to discover a divine patron that resonates with their life and vocation. The modest altar of a blacksmith to Hephaestus carries meaning equal to the noble devotion offered to Zeus.
entities.name: Variety in Divine Identity

desc: Since the times of the Vēdaḥ, there has existed the concept of one's Dharma being classified as one of the four possibles: ''Brāhmaṇa'', scholars or priests; ''Kṣatriya'', rulers or warriors; ''Vaiśya'', farmers or merchants; or ''Śūdra'', artisans or servants. These classifications are not rigid, but instead represent the ideal of an individual's calling, and they have been very influential in Hindu society.
entities.name: Varṇa System

desc: Our genius in fortification does not represent a radical departure in their design; rather, the innovation comes from the placement of the fortresses. By taking maximum advantage of local terrain, even the most basic fort requires more effort and supplies to take.
entities.name: Innovative Fortifications

desc: The Veche is a popular assembly with its origins in ancient tribal councils, which themselves existed long before the time of the Rus'. It is the highest judicial and legislative authority of the state.
entities.name: The Veche

desc: The main texts among the Śruti are the Vēdaḥ, which are the oldest Sanskrit texts. Their authorship is attributed to Brahmā in the Mahābhārata, and they are the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda.
entities.name: Vēdaḥ

desc: Although it depends on the school, there are some rules in the Dharma regarding abstinence from meat consumption. Each school has different views about the strictness of this abstinence, and also whether it should apply only to the monastic community or to the population in general.
entities.name: Vegetarianism

desc: The great palaces rising along our canals embody an architecture wholly our own — borrowing the pointed arch of the Gothic north, the open loggia of the Byzantine east, and the delicate tracery of Islamic craftsmen, fused into the style we call ''Gotico Fiorito''. Nowhere else in Italy does a merchant's wealth announce itself so confidently in stone and carved marble, and the Palazzo Ducale and the Ca' d'Oro stand as proof that our republic can raise monuments as magnificent as any king's. This architectural tradition reinforces the standing of our patrician class, making the physical face of Venice inseparable from the prosperity and civic pride that sustains it.
entities.name: Gotico Fiorito

desc: The ''Teatro La Fenice'' — the Phoenix — opened its doors in 1792 as the grandest opera house in Italy, built to replace a theatre lost to fire and named for the bird that rises from its own ashes, a symbol that would prove grimly prophetic more than once. Its gilded interior, its boxes arranged by rank, and its season of premieres turned opera from aristocratic private entertainment into the defining cultural event of a city that had run out of military victories but not beauty. This theatre gives Venice a stage on which the Republic's taste, wealth, and ambition are on display every night, reaching an audience of nobles, travellers, and critics whose admiration travels further than any diplomatic dispatch.
entities.name: La Fenice

desc: Andrea Palladio drew on the proportions of ancient Rome and the building materials of the Veneto to create a style that is simultaneously learned and practical, at home in a villa on the Brenta as in a civic loggia on a market square. His principles spread from Vicenza across every ''Terraferma'' city, giving our public buildings a dignity grounded in mathematics rather than fashion. This ''Oordine Palladiano'' not only beautifies our cities but makes them legible — a visitor entering our towns reads confidence, prosperity, and permanence in every facade.
entities.name: Palladian Architecture

desc: When Aldo Manuzio established the ''Aldine Press'' in Venice in 1494, we became the printing capital of the world almost overnight — our merchants had the gold to finance it, our scholars the Greek and Latin to edit it, and our trade routes to carry the finished books to every court in Europe. The italic typeface, the affordable pocket octavo, and the authoritative editions of Plato, Aristotle, and Virgil that Aldo produced set a standard that no press on the continent has since matched. This mastery of the book trade gives Venice a commercial and intellectual reach that extends far beyond what our galleys can carry, making the ideas that flow from our presses as valuable as the spices in our warehouses.
entities.name: Printing Industry

desc: In 1638 the Great Council of Venice took the unprecedented step of licensing a permanent public gambling house in the Palazzo Dandolo, creating the ''Ridotto'' — the first state-supervised casino in Europe. Admission required a mask and a patrician's hat, which gave the establishment the appearance of equality while ensuring that the proceeds flowed reliably to the treasury and the behavior of the nobility remained visible to the state. This managed institution transformed a vice the Republic could not suppress into a dependable source of revenue and a mechanism for keeping the city's most powerful men where they could be watched.
entities.name: Il Ridotto

desc: The aristocracy of the Veneto has made the ''Terraferma'' its summer country, building villas that are at once working farms, places of retreat, and stages for the cultural life that cannot be conducted on a canal. Along the Brenta and through the hills of Vicenza and Treviso, these estates host salons, concerts, and philosophical conversations that rival anything the academies of the cities can offer. This culture of the ''Vìla'' (''Villa'' in standard Italian: country estate) draws talent from across the region and keeps our governing class connected to the land they administer, giving them a practical knowledge that purely urban oligarchies tend to lose.
entities.name: Villa Culture of the Veneto

desc: Before Florence claimed the Renaissance as its own, the scholars of the Veneto were already recovering the texts of antiquity and asking what it means to live as a citizen rather than a subject. Francesco Petrarca spent his final years among us, and the libraries and courts of the region drew men of letters who saw no contradiction between classical learning and Christian faith. This tradition of ''Umanesimo'' shapes how our governors think — not only as administrators but as men formed by history and argument, elevating the quality of every negotiation we conduct.
entities.name: Venetian Humanism

desc: From the days of the earliest ''Doge'', Venice has built its power on the mastery of the sea — our merchants carry the riches of the East through the Adriatic while the ''Stato da Mar'', our network of overseas ports and islands, secures the routes that sustain it all. At the heart of this maritime order stands the ''Arsenale'', the greatest industrial complex of the medieval world, capable of launching a fully fitted galley in a single day when the Republic demands it. This combination of merchant dominance, state shipyard, and overseas empire makes Venice unlike any landlocked rival, transforming the sea itself into an extension of our state.
entities.name: Stato da Mar

desc: The painters of our cities have developed a style unlike any other in Italy — abandoning the hard outlines of the Florentine tradition for the warm luminosity of color and the soft blending of light that only the ''Pittura Veneziana'' commands. Giovanni Bellini, Giorgione, and Tiziano Vecelli have made our workshops the envy of every patron in Christendom, and foreign lords send commissions across the Alps because no other school can match the richness of our pigments or the confidence of our compositions. This tradition of painting gives our culture a reputation for sensory refinement that travels further than our armies, drawing patrons, wealth, and admiration from courts that we could never reach by force.
entities.name: Venetian Painting

desc: The cities of the Veneto built their wealth and order on the ''Comùn'' (''Comune'' in standard Italian: the Commune) — a covenant between burghers and nobility to share the obligations of governance rather than leave them to a single lord. From Padua to Verona and the mountain towns beyond, this tradition of elected councils, written statutes, and civic courts gave our urban life a stability and confidence that purely feudal regions could not match. This communal heritage makes our institutions resilient and our burghers invested in the success of the city they help govern.
entities.name: Communal Tradition

desc: The twin choir lofts of San Marco, facing each other across the golden nave, gave birth to the ''Cori Spesâi'' (''Cori Spezzati'' in standard Italian: Divided Choirs) technique — two ensembles answering and overlapping in a controlled interplay of sound that only the basilica's extraordinary acoustics can fully realize. Adrian Willaert, the Gabrielis, and Claudio Monteverdi all worked within this tradition, and the musicians they trained carried the Venetian polyphonic style to courts from Madrid to Vienna. This school of music makes Venice the acknowledged capital of European sound, and the stream of composers and singers our city produces carries Venetian prestige to places our galleys never reach.
entities.name: Venetian School of Music

desc: In the weeks before Lent, the cities of our culture put on the ''Bauta'' and briefly become equals — a merchant in a mask walks beside a senator and cannot be distinguished, and the rules that govern dress, movement, and address are suspended by universal consent. This tradition of supervised disorder has served us for centuries as a pressure valve, and it has drawn visitors from across Europe who spend freely while marveling at the spectacle. This annual carnival sustains our reputation for a kind of governed liberty that no other culture in Europe can quite replicate.
entities.name: Carnevale

desc: Because so many of our government positions are held by those seeking to advance themselves, we sometimes find that those who run our administration are susceptible to bribes from foreign powers. Running some simple background checks will weed out the officials most prone to corruption.
entities.name: Vetting

desc: Great minds flock to our court from across the known world, bringing with them diverse languages, fashions, and art. As a result of this exposure, we have grown more accommodating of their foreign 'manners'.
entities.name: Vibrant Court

desc: Makes it possible for us to establish Viceroys, therby improving the administration of our colonies and increase the amount of money they generate.
entities.name: Viceroys

desc: A viceroyalty refers to a distinct and semi-autonomous territorial unit within a kingdom, characterized as a monarchical state governed by a designated viceroy. These administrative entities are entrusted to a viceroy, appointed by the monarch, with the crucial responsibility of managing and governing a specific country or province. Typically situated apart from the central core of the kingdom, the viceroyalty operates as a separate entity, exhibiting a degree of self-governance while ultimately being answerable to the reigning monarch. The viceroy's role encompasses a wide range of duties, including the implementation of policies, the maintenance of order, and the representation of the king's authority in the designated region.
entities.name: Viceroyalty

desc: To finalize the transition from a medieval feudal state to a modern, centralized monarchy, the Tsardom will promulgate the ''Societas Codex Shishman'', a comprehensive legal reform that unifies the disparate local customs of the Western Balkans. This code will establish a professional judiciary independent of the local landowners and standardize the weights, measures, and currencies used throughout Vidin's trade network. By providing a predictable and fair legal environment, we will ensure the growth of a loyal urban middle class and the stability of the state's tax revenue. This administrative modernization will make Vidin a beacon of 'Enlightened Despotism' in the East, where the rule of law is as ironclad as the walls of Baba Vida itself.
entities.name: The Codex Shishman

desc: Vidin needs to expand its influence into the mineral-rich Timok valley, granting charters to Saxon and Ragusan miners to extract silver, lead, and copper. This industrial base will provide the Tsardom with the metal needed for modern currency and the production of high-quality firearms, making Vidin a self-sufficient military power. The wealth from these mines will also allow the Tsars to maintain a professional army.
entities.name: The Mining Grants

desc: To ensure the loyalty of the border nobility and create a professional officer corps, the Tsars of Vidin will establish a local knightly order modeled after the Western European ''Societas Draconistrarum''. Members of this order will be granted estates along the Timok and Danube rivers in exchange for maintaining a state of perpetual readiness and providing a heavy cavalry core for the Tsardom's defense. This institution will hopefully bridge the gap between the old Bulgarian Boyar traditions and the chivalric standards of the West, fostering a high level of military discipline and personal loyalty to the crown and prevent internal fragmentation.
entities.name: The Order of the Danubian Dragon

desc: The fortress of Vidin, situated at a strategic bend in the Danube, serves as the ultimate gateway between the Bulgarian lands, the Hungarian plains, and the Serbian mountains. Under the Shishman dynasty, the castle of Baba Vida has been transformed into a sophisticated riverine citadel capable of withstand long sieges and housing a permanent garrison of elite troops. This focus on defensive architecture ensures that Vidin remains a sovereign bastion, even when the rest of the Bulgarian heartland is under threat, acting as a 'Western Shield' for the nation.
entities.name: The Stronghold of Baba Vida

desc: Positioned at the crossroads of cultures, the Tsars of Vidin have maintained closer ties with the Catholic West than any other Bulgarian rulers, often marrying into Hungarian and Wallachian nobility. This diplomatic flexibility allows Vidin to survive as an independent state, utilizing Western military technology and courtly traditions to distinguish itself from the rest of Bulgaria. By acting as a bridge between the Orthodox and Catholic worlds, Vidin becomes a center of trade and intellectual exchange that enriches the local treasury and the army.
entities.name: The Western Connection

desc: As the trade between the upper Danube and the Black Sea grows, Vidin has become one of the most important custom houses on the Lower Danube, regulating the flow of European luxury goods into the Balkans.
